failed.question:
The owner of a home was awakened in the middle of the night by the sound of breaking glass. Erroneously concluding that he had been dreaming, the owner went back to sleep. Several minutes later, the owner was again awakened by a loud crashing sound coming from his living room. The owner grabbed a pistol that he kept by his bedside and went to investigate. In his living room, the owner saw a burglar place the owner's laptop into a bag and then watched as the burglar quickly headed for the back door of the house. Before the burglar could escape, the owner intentionally shot and killed the burglar. The owner has been charged with the murder of the burglar.
Was the owner's killing of the burglar justified?

A woman experiencing homelessness broke into the basement of a hotel and fell asleep. She was awakened by a security guard, who demanded that she leave. As the woman was leaving, she cursed the security guard. Angered, the guard began to beat the woman on her head with his flashlight. After the second blow, the woman grabbed a fire extinguisher and sprayed the guard in his face, causing him to lose his sight in one eye.
The jurisdiction defines aggravated assault as assault with intent to cause serious bodily injury.
The crimes below are listed in descending order of seriousness. What is the most serious crime of which the woman could be properly convicted?

Throughout her life, the defendant had visions of an unknown woman who told her to commit inappropriate, and sometimes violent, acts. The defendant truly believed that the unknown woman had her best interests at heart and that, therefore, whatever the woman said to do was right. The defendant had a history of self-medicating with drugs and alcohol, which helped her ignore the visions. One month, the defendant was so consistently intoxicated that she inadvertently forgot to pay her rent. When the defendant's landlord came to the door to remind her to pay, the defendant began to have visions of the unknown woman telling her to kill her landlord. The defendant grabbed a letter opener that happened to be by the front door and stabbed her landlord with it.
The defendant has been charged with second-degree murder in a jurisdiction that uses the M'Naghten test. A state statute defines second-degree murder as common-law murder.
What is the defendant's best defense against this charge?

A man who suffered from post-traumatic stress disorder became convinced that his neighbor was an evil demon. Truly believing that he needed to save the world from an evil demon, the man killed the neighbor. The man was charged with murder, and his defense attorney raised an insanity defense. During the trial, a psychiatrist testified that the man would not have killed the neighbor in the absence of his post-traumatic stress disorder and that the man did not think it was immoral to kill the neighbor because he believed the neighbor was an evil demon. The jurisdiction in which the court resides has adopted the M'Naghten test for insanity.
What is the man's strongest argument in support of an insanity defense?

questions.question:
Instead of going to work one evening, a man decided to visit a bar to watch a basketball game. The man started drinking when he arrived and quickly became intoxicated. While the man was watching the game, his girlfriend arrived at the bar. The girlfriend approached the man and began arguing with him about skipping work to drink. The man in turn accused the girlfriend of visiting the bar alone to flirt with other people. The argument escalated and the girlfriend tried to scratch the man's face. The man tried to grab the girlfriend's wrists to push her arms away, but because his intoxication made him clumsy, he accidentally pushed her backward hard enough to knock her down. The man has been charged with criminal battery.
Can the man properly be convicted of criminal battery on these facts?

choices.a: No, because the man acted justifiably.
choices.b: No, because the man's criminal behavior is excused.
choices.c: Yes, because battery is a general intent crime.
choices.d: Yes, because the man made no attempt to retreat from the altercation.

The man tried to grab the girlfriend's wrists to push her arms away, but because his intoxication made him clumsy, he accidentally pushed her backward hard enough to knock her down. The man has been charged with criminal battery.

Can the man properly be convicted of criminal battery on these facts?

一天晚上，一名男子没有去上班，而是决定去酒吧看一场篮球比赛。该男子一到酒吧就开始喝酒，并很快就醉了。在该男子看比赛时，他的女友来到了酒吧。女友走近该男子，并开始就他为了喝酒而翘班一事与他争吵。该男子反过来指责女友独自来酒吧是为了与他人调情。争吵升级，女友试图抓该男子的脸。该男子试图抓住女友的手腕以推开她的手臂，但由于醉酒导致他动作笨拙，他不小心将她向后推倒在地。该男子被控犯有刑事殴打罪(criminal battery)。

根据这些事实，该男子能否被恰当地判定犯有刑事殴打罪(criminal battery)？
options:
A. No, because the man acted justifiably.
不，因为该男子的行为具有正当性。

B. No, because the man was intoxicated.
不，因为该男子喝醉了。

C. Yes, because battery is a general intent crime.
是，因为殴打罪(battery)是一种一般意图犯罪。

D. Yes, because the man made no attempt to retreat from the altercation.
是，因为该男子没有试图从争执中退让。
data.explanation:
Self-defense


(justification for criminal conduct)General requirementsDuty to retreat
Nondeadly force
  • Actual & reasonable belief of imminent unlawful harm
  • Force reasonably necessary to prevent harm
  • Not initial aggressor
No duty to retreat
Deadly force
  • Actual & reasonable belief of imminent seriousharm or death
  • Deadly force necessary to prevent harm
  • Not initial aggressor
  • Majority rule: No duty to retreat
  • Minority rule: Duty when safe retreat available unless inside one's home
Criminal battery occurs when a person unlawfully applies force to another, resulting in bodily harm or offensive contact. However, the person's otherwise unlawful use of force may be justifiable if it is deemed socially acceptable due to the circumstances in which it occurred. For example, the application of force against another is justified if committed in self-defense—ie, if the actor:

  • actually and reasonably believed the force was necessary to protect against imminent unlawful harm

  • used reasonable force (ie, no more than necessary) to prevent such harm and

  • was not the initial aggressor - ie, did not provoke the altercation.


The reasonableness of a voluntarily intoxicated person's response to imminent unlawful harm is measured through the eyes of a reasonable, sober individual.

Here, the man's belief that force was necessary to protect himself from the girlfriend's imminent and unlawful scratching was reasonable. His use of force was also reasonable because it is likely that a reasonable, sober person also would have tried to push the girlfriend away. And since the man was not the initial aggressor, his actions constitute justifiable self-defense. As a result, he cannot properly be convicted of criminal battery.

(Choice B) Voluntary intoxication is generally not a defense to general intent crimes like criminal battery. While intoxication may serve as an excuse for the commission of a specific intent crime if it prevented the defendant from forming the requisite intent, it does not excuse the general intent required for battery. Therefore, the man's intoxication is not a valid legal reason for his acquittal.

(Choice C) Criminal battery is a general intent crime because it requires that the criminal act be consciously performed (or criminally negligent). But this fact alone does not determine the outcome; it simply establishes the required mental state. It does not negate the man's ability to successfully claim that he justifiably acted in self-defense.

(Choice D) There is no duty to retreat before using nondeadly force in self-defense (as seen here)—even if there is an opportunity to do so safely.

Educational objective: Use of force against another is justified as self-defense if the actor (1) actually and reasonably believed the force was necessary to protect against imminent unlawful harm, (2) used reasonable force to prevent such harm, and (3) was not the initial aggressor.

正当防卫


(刑事行为的正当性理由)一般要求退让义务
非致命性武力
  • 对即将发生的非法伤害有实际且合理的认知
  • 为阻止伤害而合理必要的武力
  • 非初始攻击者
无退让义务
致命性武力
  • 对即将发生的严重伤害或死亡有实际且合理的认知
  • 为阻止伤害而必要的致命性武力
  • 非初始攻击者
  • 多数规则：无退让义务
  • 少数规则：在可以安全退让时有退让义务，除非在自己家中
刑事殴打罪(Criminal battery)是指一人非法对他人施加武力，导致身体伤害或冒犯性接触。然而，如果一个人的非法使用武力行为因其发生的情境而被认为社会可接受，则该行为可能是正当的。例如，如果为了正当防卫而对他人使用武力，则是正当的——即，如果行为人：

  • 实际并合理地相信使用武力对于防范即将来临的非法伤害是必要的

  • 使用了合理的武力（即，不超过必要的限度）以阻止此类伤害，并且

  • 不是初始攻击者——即，没有挑起争执。


一个自愿醉酒者对即将来临的非法伤害所做出的反应的合理性，是通过一个理性的、清醒的个体的视角来衡量的。

在本案中，该男子认为有必要使用武力来保护自己免受女友即将来临的非法抓挠，这种看法是合理的。他使用武力也是合理的，因为一个理性的、清醒的人很可能也会试图推开女友。而且，由于该男子不是初始攻击者，他的行为构成了正当防卫。因此，他不能被恰当地判定犯有刑事殴打罪(criminal battery)。

(选项B) 自愿醉酒通常不能作为对刑事殴打罪这类一般意图犯罪的抗辩。虽然如果醉酒状态妨碍了被告形成必要的特定犯罪意图，可以作为特定意图犯罪的免责理由，但它不能免除殴打罪所要求的一般意图。因此，该男子的醉酒状态不是其被判无罪的有效法律理由。

(选项C) 刑事殴打罪是一种一般意图犯罪，因为它要求犯罪行为是有意识地实施的（或构成刑事过失）。但仅凭这一事实并不能决定案件结果；它只是确立了所要求的犯罪心理状态。它并不能否定该男子成功主张其行为属于正当防卫的能力。

(选项D) 在正当防卫中使用非致命性武力之前没有退让的义务（如本案所示）——即使有安全退让的机会也是如此。

教学目标：对他人使用武力，如果行为人（1）实际并合理地相信使用武力对于防范即将来临的非法伤害是必要的，（2）使用了合理的武力以阻止此类伤害，并且（3）不是初始攻击者，则该行为可被视为正当防卫。

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

刑法：殴打罪与正当防卫
正确答案：A

不，因为该男子的行为具有正当性 (Justification)。

本题考察的核心是正当防卫 (Self-Defense) 作为刑事责任的阻却事由，以及醉酒 (Intoxication) 对一般意图犯罪的影响。

⚖️ 核心法律规则解析
1. 刑事殴打罪 (Criminal Battery)

殴打罪属于General Intent Crime（一般意图犯罪）。它不需要被告有造成特定伤害的意图，只需要被告有意识地实施了非法的武力接触。

2. 正当防卫 (Self-Defense)

当一个人面对即将发生的非法武力时，有权使用合理且必要的武力进行自卫。

  • 非致命武力 (Non-deadly force)： 如果被告合理地认为有必要保护自己免受即将发生的非法身体伤害，可以使用非致命武力。
  • 退让义务 (Duty to Retreat)： 在使用非致命武力前，没有退让义务。
🔍 案情深度分析

为什么该男子无罪？逻辑链条如下：

  1. 威胁存在： 女友试图抓他的脸，这是即将发生的非法武力 (Imminent unlawful force)。
  2. 反应合理： 男子试图抓住她的手腕推开她。对于防止被抓脸来说，这是一种成比例的、非致命的武力。
  3. 结果归责： 虽然他因为醉酒导致动作笨拙（Clumsy），不小心把她推倒了，但他的初始行为（推开手臂）是合法的正当防卫。

在刑法中，如果行为本身是正当的 (Justified)，那么由此产生的意外结果通常不承担刑事责任，除非该防卫行为本身极其不合理或鲁莽。

❌ 干扰项陷阱排除

选项 B 错误：关于醉酒 (Intoxication)

这是一个经典的 MBE 陷阱。虽然Voluntary Intoxication（自愿醉酒）通常不能作为一般意图犯罪（如 Battery）的辩护理由，但本题的关键不是因为他醉了所以没有犯罪意图，而是因为他的行为构成了正当防卫。正当防卫是“正当化事由”(Justification)，优于醉酒问题。

选项 C 错误：关于一般意图 (General Intent)

虽然 Battery 确实是一般意图犯罪，但这只是确立了犯罪构成的心理要件。它不能否定正当防卫这一抗辩理由。如果行为是正当的，无论是什么意图类型的犯罪，都不能定罪。

选项 D 错误：关于退让义务 (Duty to Retreat)

法律规定，在使用非致命武力（如推搡、抓手腕）进行自卫时，被告没有义务先试图逃跑或退让，即使他可以安全地这样做。

💡 MBE 考试技巧

在处理涉及“醉酒”和“自卫”混合的题目时：

  • 首先判断行为是否符合正当防卫的客观标准（是否有威胁？武力是否对等？）。
  • 如果符合正当防卫，那么无论被告是否醉酒，通常都无罪。
  • 不要看到“醉酒”就立刻套用“自愿醉酒不抗辩一般意图犯罪”的规则，要先看行为的正当性 (Justification)。

questions.question:
A man started a large fire on the back acreage of his expansive rural property, which borders a fertilizer plant. A witness told police that the man started the fire to clear brush from his property. As a result, the man was charged with violating a state statute making it a crime to "recklessly create a risk of widespread injury or damage in the employment of fire, explosives, or other dangerous means." At trial, the prosecutor called the witness who testified that she watched the man set the fire less than 50 yards from the fertilizer plant. The witness also unexpectedly testified that, while starting the fire, the man stated that he intended it to spread to the fertilizer plant because he hated the plant owner.
The jurisdiction has adopted the Model Penal Code with regard to mens rea.
If the jury believes the witness's testimony, can the man be properly convicted based upon the evidence presented at trial?

choices.a: No, because the testimony established a purposeful rather than reckless mental state, which is required for conviction.
choices.b: No, because the man started the fire on his own property.
choices.c: Yes, because the man acted purposely.
choices.d: Yes, because the witness described a reckless mental state.

data.questionStem:
Q85096

A man started a large fire on the back acreage of his expansive rural property, which borders a fertilizer plant. A witness told police that the man started the fire to clear brush from his property. As a result, the man was charged with violating a state statute making it a crime to "recklessly create a risk of widespread injury or damage in the employment of fire, explosives, or other dangerous means." At trial, the prosecutor called the witness who testified that she watched the man set the fire less than 50 yards from the fertilizer plant. The witness also unexpectedly testified that, while starting the fire, the man stated that he intended it to spread to the fertilizer plant because he hated the plant owner.

The jurisdiction has adopted the Model Penal Code with regard to mens rea.

If the jury believes the witness's testimony, can the man be properly convicted based upon the evidence presented at trial?

一名男子在他广阔的乡村地产的后方面积上放了一场大火，该地产与一家化肥厂接壤。一名证人告诉警方，该男子放火是为了清理他地产上的灌木丛。因此，该男子被指控违反了一项州法规，该法规规定“在使用火、爆炸物或其他危险手段时，鲁莽地（recklessly）造成广泛伤害或损害的风险”构成犯罪。在审判中，检察官传唤了证人，证人作证说，她看到该男子在距离化肥厂不到50码的地方放火。证人还出乎意料地作证说，该男子在放火时声称，他意图让火势蔓延到化肥厂，因为他憎恨化肥厂的所有者。

该司法管辖区在犯罪意图（mens rea）方面采用了《模范刑法典》(Model Penal Code)。

如果陪审团相信证人的证词，根据庭审中出示的证据，该男子是否可以被正式定罪？
options:
A. No, because the testimony established a purposeful rather than reckless mental state, which is required for conviction.
不可以，因为证词证实被告具有故意（purposeful）而非鲁莽（reckless）的主观心态，而定罪要求的是鲁莽。

B. No, because the man started the fire on his own property.
不可以，因为该男子是在自己的地产上放火。

C. Yes, because the man acted purposely.
可以，因为该男子的行为是故意的（purposely）。

D. Yes, because the witness described a reckless mental state.
可以，因为证人描述了一种鲁莽的（reckless）主观心态。
data.explanation:
The Model Penal Code utilizes the following hierarchy of culpable mental states:


purposelyacting with a conscious objective to engage in conduct or to cause a particular result
knowinglyacting with awareness that conduct is of the nature required by a crime or with practical certainty that conduct will cause a particular result
recklesslyacting with a conscious disregard of a substantial and unjustifiable risk amounting to a gross deviation from the standard of conduct a law-abiding citizen would exhibit
negligentlyacting with a lack of awareness of a substantial and unjustifiable risk amounting to a gross deviation from the standard of care a reasonable person would exhibit
When an offense requires proof that the defendant acted with a particular mental state (ie, mens rea), evidence that the defendant actually possessed a more culpable mental state will satisfy the mens rea requirement. That is because a more culpable mental state naturally encompasses a lesser one.

Here, the man was charged with recklessly creating a risk of widespread injury or damage by starting a large fire near a fertilizer plant. The witness's testimony at trial showed that the man purposely created the risk of widespread injury or damage because he intended for the fire to spread to the fertilizer plant (Choice D). Since purposely is a more culpable mental state than recklessly, the man can be properly convicted (Choice A).

(Choice B) The statute provides no protection for a defendant who created the risk of widespread injury or damage from his own property. Therefore, this is not a basis to acquit the man.

Educational objective: When an offense requires that the defendant acted with a particular mental state, evidence that the defendant actually possessed a more culpable mental state will satisfy the mens rea requirement for the offense.



选项正确率统计：A选项 13%，B选项 1%，C选项 59%（正确选项），D选项 26%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

《模范刑法典》(Model Penal Code) 使用以下可归责的主观心态层级：


故意的（purposely）以实施某行为或导致某特定结果为有意识的目标而行动
明知的（knowingly）在意识到行为具有犯罪所要求的性质，或在实际确定行为将导致特定结果的情况下行动
鲁莽的（recklessly）有意识地漠视一个重大且无理的风险，该风险严重偏离了守法公民应有的行为标准
过失的（negligently）在未意识到一个重大且无理的风险的情况下行动，该风险严重偏离了理性人应有的注意标准
当一项犯罪要求证明被告具有特定的主观心态（即犯罪意图，mens rea）时，如果证据表明被告实际上具有更可归责的主观心态，则该证据将满足犯罪意图的要求。这是因为更可归责的主观心态自然包含了较轻微的主观心态。

在本案中，该男子被指控因在化肥厂附近放了一场大火而鲁莽地（recklessly）造成了广泛伤害或损害的风险。庭审中证人的证词表明，该男子是故意地（purposely）制造了广泛伤害或损害的风险，因为他意图让火势蔓延到化肥厂（选项D）。由于故意（purposely）是比鲁莽（recklessly）更可归责的主观心态，因此该男子可以被正式定罪（选项A）。

（选项B）对于在自己地产上制造广泛伤害或损害风险的被告，该法规未提供任何保护。因此，这不能作为该男子无罪的依据。

教学目标：当一项犯罪要求被告具有特定的主观心态时，如果证据表明被告实际上具有更可归责的主观心态，则该证据将满足该项犯罪的犯罪意图要求。

References

Model Penal Code § 2.02(5) (substitutes for negligence, recklessness, and knowledge).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

刑法：犯罪意图 (Mens Rea)
⚖️ 核心法律原则 根据《模范刑法典》(Model Penal Code, MPC) § 2.02(5)，当法律规定某种犯罪需要特定的主观心态（如鲁莽 Recklessness）时，如果证据证明被告实际上具有更高层级的可归责心态（如故意 Purpose 或明知 Knowledge），则该证据足以满足定罪要求。
MPC 意图层级 (Hierarchy of Culpability)

层级越高，罪责越重。高层级心态自动包含低层级心态。

1. 蓄意/故意 (Purposely)
最高层级：以造成结果为目标
↓ 包含 ↓
2. 明知 (Knowingly)
几乎确定结果会发生
↓ 包含 ↓
3. 鲁莽 (Recklessly)
本案指控标准：漠视重大风险
↓ 包含 ↓
4. 过失 (Negligently)
应当意识到风险但未意识到
🔍 案情应用
  • 指控要求：法规要求证明被告是鲁莽地 (Recklessly) 造成风险。
  • 实际证据：证人作证称被告说他意图 (Intended/Purposely) 让火蔓延到化肥厂。
  • 结论：既然被告是“蓄意”的，他的恶性程度已经超过了“鲁莽”。在法律上，证明了“蓄意”就自动满足了“鲁莽”的要求。
✅ 正确答案解析

选项 C 正确。

因为该男子是故意 (Purposely) 行事的。虽然法规只要求鲁莽，但证明被告具有更高的犯罪意图（故意）并不会让他免罪，反而更确凿地满足了定罪标准。

错误选项排除
  • 选项 A 错误：它错误地认为证明了更高的意图（故意）反而不能定罪。法律逻辑是“举重以明轻”，而非“因为太坏了所以无罪”。
  • 选项 D 错误：虽然结论是对的（可以定罪），但理由有误。证人描述的是故意的心态，而不仅仅是鲁莽。
  • 选项 B 错误：在自己土地上放火并不能成为危害公共安全或他人财产的抗辩理由。
💡 MBE 提分技巧：
遇到 MPC 的题目时，记住这个公式：
Purpose > Knowledge > Recklessness > Negligence
如果题目问“能否以 [低层级意图] 定罪？”，而事实证明了 [高层级意图]，答案永远是 YES。

"The greater culpability includes the lesser."

A defendant was charged with battery, defined as at common law. At trial, an expert witness testified for the defense that the defendant, an athlete, was under the influence of a performance-enhancing drug at the time he committed the battery and that he would not have done so had he not been so influenced. The defendant asked for an instruction to the effect that if the jury believed that he was influenced by the drug at the time of the crime and would not have committed it otherwise, it had to acquit him.
Which of the following circumstances would most aid the defendant's argument in favor of such an instruction?

choices.a: Evidence that the defendant is addicted to this drug and has an overwhelming urge to consume it.
choices.b: Evidence that the defendant's coach, who gave him the drug, told him it was only an aspirin.
choices.c: Evidence that the victim of the assault taunted the defendant about his use of the drug immediately before the assault.
choices.d: Expert testimony that a reasonable person, on consuming this drug, may experience uncontrollable rages.

Q85139

A defendant was charged with battery, defined as at common law. At trial, an expert witness testified for the defense that the defendant, an athlete, was under the influence of a performance-enhancing drug at the time he committed the battery and that he would not have done so had he not been so influenced. The defendant asked for an instruction to the effect that if the jury believed that he was influenced by the drug at the time of the crime and would not have committed it otherwise, it had to acquit him.

Which of the following circumstances would most aid the defendant's argument in favor of such an instruction?

一名被告被控犯有普通法所定义的伤害罪（battery）。在庭审中，一名专家证人为辩方作证称，身为运动员的被告在实施伤害罪时，正处在一种运动表现增强药物的影响之下，若非如此，他本不会犯下此罪。被告请求法官作出指示，大意是：如果陪审团相信被告在犯罪时受到了药物的影响，且若非如此他本不会犯罪，那么陪审团必须宣告他无罪。

以下哪种情况最能支持被告提出该项指示的论点？
options:
A. Evidence that the defendant is addicted to this drug and has an overwhelming urge to consume it.
证据表明，被告对该药物成瘾，并有强烈的服用欲望。

B. Evidence that the defendant's coach, who gave him the drug, told him it was only an aspirin.
证据表明，给被告药物的教练告诉他，那只是阿司匹林。

C. Evidence that the victim of the assault taunted the defendant about his use of the drug immediately before the assault.
证据表明，在伤害行为发生前夕，受害人就被告使用药物一事对其进行了嘲讽。

D. Expert testimony that a reasonable person, on consuming this drug, may experience uncontrollable rages.
专家证词表明，一个理性人在服用此药物后，可能会经历无法控制的暴怒。
data.explanation:
An intoxication defense can be raised if the defendant was intoxicated when the charged crime was committed due to either of the following:

  • Involuntary intoxication - the unknowing or forcible ingestion of an intoxicating substance is a defense to any crime if it placed the defendant in the mental state required for an insanity defense.
  • Voluntary intoxication - the deliberate ingestion of a substance that the defendant knew or should have known has intoxicating effects is a defense to specific intent crimes if it prevented the defendant from forming such intent.


Here, the defendant requested an instruction that the jury acquit him if it believed that he was influenced by the performance-enhancing drug when he committed the battery and would not have done so otherwise. Since battery is a general intent crime, that instruction would only be proper if the intoxication was involuntary . Therefore, evidence that the defendant's coach tricked him into taking the drug by telling him that it was aspirin would support such an instruction.

(Choice A) Voluntary intoxication is never a defense to general intent crimes like battery. And evidence that the defendant was addicted to the drug would not make his ingestion involuntary (ie, unknowing or forcible) for purposes of criminal law. Therefore, this evidence would not support an intoxication instruction.

(Choice C) The fact that the victim taunted the defendant about his use of the drug immediately before the crime would not serve as a defense to a battery charge or support an intoxication instruction.

(Choice D) Expert testimony that the drug causes uncontrollable rage would not support an intoxication instruction since voluntary intoxication - regardless of the intoxicant's effects - is no defense to battery.

Educational objective: Involuntary intoxication is a defense to any crime if it placed the defendant in the mental state required for an insanity defense. And voluntary intoxication is a defense to specific intent crimes if it prevented the defendant from forming the required intent.



选项正确率统计：A选项 0%，B选项 82%（正确选项），C选项 0%，D选项 16%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

如果被告在实施被指控的罪行时因以下任一原因而处于醉态，可以提出醉态辩护（intoxication defense）：

  • 非自愿醉态（Involuntary intoxication） - 在不知情或被强迫的情况下摄入致醉物质，如果这使被告的精神状态达到了精神错乱辩护（insanity defense）所要求的程度，那么它可以作为对任何犯罪的辩护理由。
  • 自愿醉态（Voluntary intoxication） - 故意摄入被告知道或理应知道具有致醉效果的物质，如果这种醉态使被告无法形成特定意图，那么它可以作为对特定意图犯罪（specific intent crimes）的辩护理由。


在本案中，被告请求法官作出指示，如果陪审团相信他在实施伤害罪时受到了运动表现增强药物的影响，并且若非如此他本不会这样做，则应宣告其无罪。由于伤害罪是一项一般意图犯罪（general intent crime），只有当醉态是非自愿的情况下，该指示才是恰当的。因此，能证明被告的教练欺骗他服用药物并告诉他那是阿司匹林的证据，将支持这样一项指示。

(选项A) 对于像伤害罪这样的一般意图犯罪，自愿醉态从来都不是辩护理由。并且，从刑法的角度来看，被告对药物成瘾的证据并不能使其摄入行为成为非自愿的（即不知情或被强迫的）。因此，这项证据不支持关于醉态辩护的指示。

(选项C) 受害人在犯罪前夕因被告使用药物而对其进行嘲讽，这一事实不能作为对伤害罪指控的辩护理由，也不能支持关于醉态辩护的指示。

(选项D) 专家证词表明该药物会导致无法控制的暴怒，但这并不能支持关于醉态辩护的指示，因为自愿醉态——无论致醉物质的效果如何——都不能作为对伤害罪的辩护理由。

教学目标：如果非自愿醉态使被告的精神状态达到了精神错乱辩护所要求的程度，那么它可以作为对任何犯罪的辩护理由。而自愿醉态如果阻碍了被告形成所需的意图，则可以作为对特定意图犯罪的辩护理由。

MBE 刑法考点解析

Intoxication Defense (醉态辩护)
核心法则：醉态与犯罪意图

在普通法（Common Law）中，醉态辩护的有效性取决于两个因素的组合：

  1. 醉态的类型：自愿（Voluntary） vs. 非自愿（Involuntary）。
  2. 犯罪的类型：一般意图（General Intent） vs. 特定意图（Specific Intent）。

第一步：定性犯罪类型
本题中的指控是 Battery（殴打/伤害罪）。在普通法中，Battery 属于典型的一般意图犯罪（General Intent Crime）。

第二步：应用规则
对于一般意图犯罪：

  • × 自愿醉态：不能作为辩护理由。无论被告醉得多厉害，只要是自愿摄入的，法律推定其具有一般犯罪意图。
  • ✓ 非自愿醉态：可以作为辩护理由。如果醉态导致被告符合精神错乱（Insanity）的标准，则可宣告无罪。

第三步：寻找“非自愿”证据
被告想要获得无罪指示（acquittal instruction），必须证明他的醉态是非自愿的（Involuntary）。

正确答案：选项 B

"证据表明，给被告药物的教练告诉他，那只是阿司匹林。"

法律依据：非自愿醉态（Involuntary Intoxication）通常发生在以下情况：

  1. 不知情（Unknowingly）：被告不知道自己摄入的是致醉物质（例如本选项，被欺骗以为是阿司匹林）。
  2. 被强迫（Under Duress）：被告在威胁下被迫摄入。

因为教练的欺骗，被告摄入药物属于“非自愿”。如果这种非自愿的醉态导致他无法控制行为（符合精神错乱标准），这对于 Battery 这样的一般意图犯罪也是有效的辩护。

选项 A：成瘾 (Addiction)

错误原因：在刑法中，成瘾者基于瘾癖摄入药物仍被视为自愿（Voluntary）行为。除非是病理性醉态等极少数例外，否则成瘾不能将醉态转化为非自愿。

选项 D：导致暴怒 (Uncontrollable Rages)

错误原因：这描述的是药物的效果，而不是摄入的性质。如果摄入是自愿的（Voluntary），即使药物导致了不可控的暴怒，也不能为一般意图犯罪（Battery）辩护。

💡 MBE 解题技巧

看到“醉态辩护”（Intoxication）题目时，请按以下流程思考：

  1. 看罪名：是 Specific Intent（如 Burglary, Larceny, First-degree Murder）还是 General Intent（如 Battery, Arson, Rape）？
  2. 看醉态：是自愿喝的，还是被骗/被逼喝的？
  3. 配对：
    • 自愿醉态 ➔ 只能辩护 Specific Intent。
    • 非自愿醉态 ➔ 可辩护所有犯罪（包括 General Intent）。

questions.question:
A man was paroled after serving five years in prison for forgery. Three weeks later, he found a handgun in a high school parking lot. Fearing that students from the school might find the gun and get into trouble using it, the man put it in the trunk of his car. The man drove off, was lawfully stopped by a police officer for speeding, and allowed the officer to search his car and the trunk. During the search, the officer discovered the gun.
The man was charged under a federal statute prohibiting the knowing possession of a firearm by a convicted felon.
Which of the following additional facts, if established, would be most helpful to the man's defense?

choices.a: He did not intend to use the gun for an unlawful purpose.
choices.b: He did not know about the federal statute.
choices.c: He was driving to the police station to give the gun to the authorities when the officer stopped his car.
choices.d: His previous conviction did not involve the use of a gun or other weapon.

data.questionStem:
Q84812 A man was paroled after serving five years in prison for forgery. Three weeks later, he found a handgun in a high school parking lot. Fearing that students from the school might find the gun and get into trouble using it, the man put it in the trunk of his car. The man drove off, was lawfully stopped by a police officer for speeding, and allowed the officer to search his car and the trunk. During the search, the officer discovered the gun.

The man was charged under a federal statute prohibiting the knowing possession of a firearm by a convicted felon.

Which of the following additional facts, if established, would be most helpful to the man's defense? 一名男子因伪造罪服刑五年后获得假释。三周后，他在一所高中的停车场发现了一把手枪。由于担心该校学生可能会发现这把枪并用它惹上麻烦，该男子便将其放入了汽车后备箱。该男子开车离开时，因超速被一名警官合法拦下，并允许警官搜查他的汽车和后备箱。在搜查过程中，警官发现了这把枪。

该男子根据一项禁止被定罪的重罪犯明知而持有枪支的联邦法规被起诉。

如果以下哪一项额外事实得以证实，将对该男子的辩护最有帮助？
options:
A. He did not intend to use the gun for an unlawful purpose.
他无意将该枪支用于非法目的。

B. He did not know about the federal statute.
他不知道有这项联邦法规。

C. He was driving to the police station to give the gun to the authorities when the officer stopped his car.
当警官拦下他的车时，他正开车前往警察局，准备将枪支交给当局。

D. His previous conviction did not involve the use of a gun or other weapon.
他之前的定罪不涉及使用枪支或其他武器。

Justifications for criminal acts


NecessityReasonable belief that conduct was necessary to avoid imminent & substantial harm
No reasonable legal alternative
Harm caused < harm avoided
Self-defenseActual & reasonable belief that harm is imminent
Reasonable force used to prevent harm
Not initial aggressor
Defense of othersActual & reasonable belief that force is necessary to protect victim from imminent harm
Reasonable force used to protect victim
Defense of propertyForce reasonably necessary to prevent imminent & unlawful interference with possessed property
Nondeadly force used
Law enforcementPrevent imminent crime
Make lawful arrest or
Prevent suspect's escape from custody
Resisting arrestReasonable force permitted to resist unlawful arrest or arrest by unknown police officer
The man violated the federal statute making it a crime for a convicted felon to knowingly possess a firearm. But the man only took the gun because he was worried that students might find the gun in the school parking lot and use it. Therefore, he can justify his criminal conduct and escape criminal liability if he can show that the crime was brought about by necessity. This requires proof that:
  • he reasonably believed that the crime was necessary to avoid imminent and substantial harm
  • no reasonable legal alternative was available and
  • the harm caused by the criminal conduct was less than the harm avoided (ie, the lesser of two evils).
Necessity must exist at all times that the defendant is engaged in the criminal conduct. Therefore, the fact that the man was driving to the police station to give the gun to the authorities when he was stopped would be most helpful to his defense.

(Choice A) The statute imposes criminal liability for knowingly possessing a firearm—even if there was no intent to use the gun for an unlawful purpose.

(Choice B) Ignorance of the law is almost never a defense. Therefore, the man's lack of knowledge about the federal statute will not absolve him of criminal liability.

(Choice D) The statute applies to all convicted felons—regardless of whether their prior conviction involved the use of a gun or other weapon.

Educational objective: Necessity justifies criminal conduct if (1) the defendant reasonably believed that such conduct was necessary to avoid imminent and substantial harm, (2) no reasonable legal alternative was available, and (3) the harm caused was less than the harm avoided.

为犯罪行为辩护的理由


紧急避险 (Necessity)合理地相信该行为对于避免迫在眉睫的重大损害是必要的
没有合理的法律替代方案
造成的损害 < 避免的损害
正当防卫 (Self-defense)实际且合理地相信损害迫在眉睫
为防止损害而使用合理的武力
非最初的攻击者
为他人防卫 (Defense of others)实际且合理地相信为保护受害人免受迫在眉睫的损害，使用武力是必要的
为保护受害人而使用合理的武力
财产防卫 (Defense of property)为防止对所占有财产的迫在眉睫的非法干涉而合理必要的武力
使用非致命性武力
执法 (Law enforcement)防止迫在眉睫的犯罪
进行合法逮捕 或
防止嫌疑人脱离羁押
拒捕 (Resisting arrest)允许使用合理的武力抵抗非法逮捕或身份不明的警官的逮捕
该男子违反了联邦法规，该法规规定被定罪的重罪犯明知而持有枪支构成犯罪。但该男子拿走枪支只是因为他担心学生可能会在学校停车场发现枪支并使用它。因此，如果他能证明该罪行是出于紧急避险 (necessity)，他就可以为自己的犯罪行为辩护 (justify) 并免除刑事责任。这需要证明：
  • 他合理地相信该犯罪行为对于避免迫在眉睫的重大损害是必要的
  • 当时没有合理的法律替代方案可供选择 并且
  • 犯罪行为造成的损害小于所避免的损害（即两害相权取其轻）。
紧急避险必须在被告从事犯罪行为的所有时间内都存在。因此，当该男子被拦下时，他正开车前往警察局将枪支交给当局这一事实，对他的辩护最有帮助。

(选项A) 该法规对明知而持有枪支的行为施加刑事责任——即使行为人无意将枪支用于非法目的。

(选项B) 不知法几乎从来都不是一种抗辩理由。因此，该男子不了解该联邦法规并不能免除其刑事责任。

(选项D) 该法规适用于所有被定罪的重罪犯——无论他们之前的定罪是否涉及使用枪支或其他武器。

教学目标： 如果(1)被告合理地相信该行为对于避免迫在眉睫的重大损害是必要的，(2)没有合理的法律替代方案，并且(3)造成的损害小于所避免的损害，则紧急避险可为犯罪行为提供正当性辩护。

MBE 刑法考点解析

Criminal Law: Defenses
⚖️ 核心考点：紧急避险 (Necessity)

当被告人为了避免迫在眉睫且更严重的伤害 (Imminent and greater harm) 而被迫实施犯罪行为，且没有其他合理的法律替代方案时，可以主张紧急避险作为辩护理由。

为何选 C 是最有力的辩护？
正确答案 C

事实：当警官拦下他的车时，他正开车前往警察局，准备将枪支交给当局。

本题涉及的罪名是重罪犯持有枪支 (Felon-in-possession)。从表面上看，该男子确实满足了犯罪构成要件：(1) 有重罪前科，(2) 明知而持有枪支。

然而，紧急避险 (Necessity) 是一种正当化事由 (Justification)。要成功运用此辩护，尤其是在持有违禁品的案件中，被告必须证明：

  • 他持有枪支是为了防止更大的伤害（学生捡到枪发生危险）；
  • 这种持有是暂时的 (Temporary)；
  • 持有仅仅是为了处理或上交该违禁品。

选项 C 提供了最关键的证据：他正在去警察局的路上。这证明了他的持有行为与“消除危险”这一紧急避险目的直接相关，且一旦危险解除（交给警察），持有即终止。如果没有这一事实，他的持有可能会被视为在危险消除后仍然继续，从而失去紧急避险的保护。

为何其他选项无效？
选项 A (无非法目的)：
该法规禁止的是“明知持有”(Knowing possession)，而非“意图非法使用”。这属于一般意图 (General Intent) 或特定状态犯罪，不需要证明被告有特定的犯罪目的。
选项 B (不知法)：
不知法不免责 (Ignorance of the law is no excuse)。除非法规本身要求被告必须知道自己违反了法律（极少见），否则不知道该联邦法规的存在不是抗辩理由。
选项 D (前科非暴力)：
联邦法规通常禁止所有被定罪的重罪犯持有枪支，并不区分之前的重罪是否涉及暴力或武器。
💡MBE 考试技巧

在处理持有类犯罪 (Possession Crimes) 的辩护题时，请注意区分“瞬间持有”与“持续持有”。

如果题目暗示被告是为了公共安全而暂时控制违禁品，并正在积极寻求将其移交给执法部门，这通常会触发紧急避险 (Necessity) 辩护。关键在于“两害相权取其轻” (Lesser of two evils)。

questions.question:
The chief executive officer (CEO) of a company that operated a knitting mill delegated all operational decision-making to the supervisor of the mill. The child labor laws in the jurisdiction provide, "It is a violation of the law for one to employ a person under the age of 17 years for full-time labor."
Without the CEO's knowledge, the supervisor hired a number of 15- and 16-year-olds to work at the mill full time. He did not ask their ages and they did not disclose them. The supervisor could have discovered their ages easily by asking for identification, but he did not do so because he was not aware of the law and believed that company policy was to hire young people.
If the statute is interpreted to create strict liability and the CEO is convicted of violating it, is his contention that his conviction would violate the Constitution correct or incorrect?

choices.a: Correct, because criminal liability is personal and the knitting mill, not the CEO, is the employer of the children.
choices.b: Correct, because it is a violation of due process to punish without a voluntary act.
choices.c: Incorrect, because he was in a position to exercise control over the hiring of employees for the knitting mill.
choices.d: Incorrect, because regulatory offenses are not subject to due process limitations.

data.questionStem:
Q85104

The chief executive officer (CEO) of a company that operated a knitting mill delegated all operational decision-making to the supervisor of the mill. The child labor laws in the jurisdiction provide, "It is a violation of the law for one to employ a person under the age of 17 years for full-time labor."

Without the CEO's knowledge, the supervisor hired a number of 15- and 16-year-olds to work at the mill full time. He did not ask their ages and they did not disclose them. The supervisor could have discovered their ages easily by asking for identification, but he did not do so because he was not aware of the law and believed that company policy was to hire young people.

If the statute is interpreted to create strict liability and the CEO is convicted of violating it, is his contention that his conviction would violate the Constitution correct or incorrect?

一家经营针织厂的公司的首席执行官（CEO）将所有运营决策权授予了该厂的主管。该司法管辖区的童工法规定：‘雇佣未满17周岁者从事全职工作属违法行为。’

在CEO不知情的情况下，该主管雇佣了数名15岁和16岁的青少年在该厂从事全职工作。他没有询问他们的年龄，他们也没有透露。主管本可以通过要求出示身份证明轻易发现他们的年龄，但他没有这样做，因为他不知道这项法律，并认为公司的政策是雇佣年轻人。

如果该法规被解释为创设严格责任，且CEO因此被定罪，那么他主张其定罪违反宪法，此主张是否正确？
options:
A. Correct, because criminal liability is personal and the knitting mill, not the CEO, is the employer of the children.
正确，因为刑事责任是个人责任，针织厂才是儿童的雇主，而非CEO。

B. Correct, because it is a violation of due process to punish without a voluntary act.
正确，因为在没有自愿行为的情况下进行处罚违反了正当程序。

C. Incorrect, because he was in a position to exercise control over the hiring of employees for the knitting mill.
不正确，因为他有权对针织厂的员工雇佣行使控制权。

D. Incorrect, because regulatory offenses are not subject to due process limitations.
不正确，因为监管性违法行为不受正当程序限制。
data.explanation:
Comparing theories of criminal liability


TheoryMens rea (criminal mind)Actus reus (criminal act)
Direct liabilityDefendant has mens reaDefendant performs actus reus
Vicarious liabilityDefendant's agent has mens reaAgent performs actus reus under defendant's control
Strict liabilityNo mens rea requirementDefendant performs actus reus
A defendant can be:
  • directly liable for a criminal act that he/she personally performed or
  • vicariously liable for a criminal act performed by another - often an employee.


But for a defendant to be convicted based on vicarious liability, due process requires proof that the defendant had control over the other's conduct. Such proof exists here because the CEO was in a position to exercise control over the supervisor's hiring practices. As a result, the CEO's vicarious liability for the supervisor's criminal hiring does not raise any due process or other constitutional concerns.

(Choice A) Criminal liability often arises when the defendant personally commits a criminal act - but not always. As in this case, a defendant can be criminally liable for failing to prevent a criminal act that an agent (eg, the supervisor) committed while under the defendant's control.

(Choice B) Due process allows punishment without a voluntary act on the part of the defendant when, as here, the defendant had control over and is being held vicariously liable for another's conduct.

(Choice D) Regulatory offenses are strict liability crimes that are designed to protect the public welfare (eg, speeding, public intoxication). These offenses are subject to due process limitations - eg, the punishment must fit the crime. And since regulatory offenses require no proof of fault, they generally are only punishable by fine.

Educational objective: Due process requires proof that the defendant had control over another's conduct to hold the defendant vicariously liable for that person's criminal act.

选项正确率统计：A选项 7%，B选项 6%，C选项 77%（正确选项），D选项 8%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

刑事责任理论比较


理论Mens rea (犯罪意图)Actus reus (犯罪行为)
直接责任被告人具有犯罪意图被告人实施犯罪行为
替代责任被告人的代理人具有犯罪意图代理人在被告人的控制下实施犯罪行为
严格责任无犯罪意图要求被告人实施犯罪行为
被告人可能：
  • 因其亲自实施的犯罪行为而承担直接责任，或者
  • 因他人（通常是雇员）实施的犯罪行为而承担替代责任。


但要基于替代责任判定被告人有罪，正当程序要求证明被告人对他人的行为拥有控制权。本案中存在此类证明，因为CEO有权对主管的雇佣行为行使控制权。因此，CEO对主管的犯罪性雇佣行为承担替代责任，并不引发任何正当程序或其他宪法上的问题。

(选项 A) 刑事责任通常在被告人亲自实施犯罪行为时产生——但并非总是如此。如此案所示，当代理人（例如，主管）在被告人控制下实施犯罪行为时，被告人可能因未能阻止该行为而承担刑事责任。

(选项 B) 当被告人对他人行为拥有控制权并因此承担替代责任时，如此案所示，正当程序允许在被告人没有自愿行为的情况下对其进行处罚。

(选项 D) 监管性违法行为是旨在保护公共福祉的严格责任犯罪（例如，超速、公共场所醉酒）。这些违法行为确实受正当程序限制——例如，罚当其罪。并且，由于监管性违法行为无需证明过错，通常仅处以罚款。

教学目标： 正当程序要求，要使被告人对他人犯罪行为承担替代责任，须证明被告人对该他人的行为拥有控制权。

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

替代责任与企业高管责任
核心考点：替代责任 (Vicarious Liability)

在涉及公共福利（Public Welfare）的严格责任犯罪（Strict Liability Crimes）中，如果公司高管拥有防止违规行为发生的权力或控制权，即使他们没有亲自实施犯罪行为，也可能需要承担刑事责任。

为什么 CEO 的主张不正确？

本题的核心在于正当程序条款 (Due Process Clause) 与替代责任之间的平衡。

通常，刑事责任要求被告有犯罪意图 (Mens Rea) 和犯罪行为 (Actus Reus)。然而，在监管性犯罪（如童工法、食品药品安全）中，法律倾向于施加严格责任。

逻辑推演：

  1. 控制权即责任： CEO 虽然将决策权下放，但他作为公司最高负责人，依然处于能够行使控制权 (Position to exercise control) 的地位。
  2. 未能履职： 他有能力建立合规机制或监督下属，但他没有这样做。
  3. 合宪性： 美国最高法院认为，对于此类旨在保护公众（特别是弱势群体如儿童）的法律，只要被告人与违规行为之间存在“负责任的关系” (Responsible Relation)，即被告人有权力和能力防止违规，那么对其定罪并不违反宪法正当程序。
⚖️ 经典判例：United States v. Park (1975)

在此案中，最高法院确立了“负责任的公司高管原则” (Responsible Corporate Officer Doctrine)。法院裁定，如果公司高管在公司体系中有权力和责任防止或纠正违法行为，但未能做到，他们可以因下属的严格责任违法行为而被追究个人刑事责任。

选项辨析

✅ 选项 C 正确： 直接切中要害。CEO 被定罪的宪法基础在于他处于能够控制雇佣行为的地位。正当程序要求的是“控制权”作为替代责任的基础。

❌ 选项 A 错误： 刑事责任并非只能是“个人的”。替代责任允许在特定情况下（如雇主-雇员关系）将一人的行为归责于另一人。

❌ 选项 B 错误： 虽然通常需要“自愿行为” (Voluntary Act)，但在替代责任中，被告的“不作为”（未能行使监督权）结合其下属的自愿行为，足以构成定罪基础。

❌ 选项 D 错误： 这种说法太绝对。监管性犯罪仍然受正当程序限制（例如刑罚必须适度），只是在本题的具体情境下，定罪本身不违宪。

💡 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)
当遇到 CEO/高管因下属违反“公共福利法规”（如健康、安全、劳工）而被起诉的题目时：

1. 检查是否为严格责任犯罪。
2. 寻找高管是否有监督/控制权力（即使他不知道具体违规）。
3. 如果有权力但未阻止 ➡️ 有罪 (Guilty)。

不要被“他不知道”或“他下放了权力”这类事实误导。

questions.question:
While walking home one evening, an off-duty police officer was accosted by a stranger. The stranger had been drinking and mistakenly thought the officer was a man who was having an affair with his wife. Intending to frighten the officer but not to harm him, the stranger pulled out a knife, screamed obscenities, and told the officer he was going to kill him. Frightened and reasonably believing the stranger was going to kill him and that using deadly force was his only salvation, the officer took out his service revolver and shot and killed the stranger.
The officer is charged with murder. At trial, he claims that he acted in self-defense.
Was the officer justified in using deadly force in self-defense?

choices.a: No, because the officer was not defending his home and had an obligation to retreat or to repel with less than deadly force.
choices.b: No, because the stranger did not in fact intend to harm the officer and the officer was incorrect in believing that he did.
choices.c: Yes, because the killing was in hot blood upon sufficient provocation.
choices.d: Yes, because the officer reasonably believed the stranger was planning to kill him and that deadly force was required.

data.questionStem:
Q85136

While walking home one evening, an off-duty police officer was accosted by a stranger. The stranger had been drinking and mistakenly thought the officer was a man who was having an affair with his wife. Intending to frighten the officer but not to harm him, the stranger pulled out a knife, screamed obscenities, and told the officer he was going to kill him. Frightened and reasonably believing the stranger was going to kill him and that using deadly force was his only salvation, the officer took out his service revolver and shot and killed the stranger.

The officer is charged with murder. At trial, he claims that he acted in self-defense.

Was the officer justified in using deadly force in self-defense?

一天晚上，一名下班的警官在回家的路上被一个陌生人纠缠。该陌生人喝了酒，并误认为该警官是与他妻子有染的男人。为了恐吓警官但无意伤害他，陌生人拔出一把刀，大声辱骂，并告诉警官他要杀了他。警官感到害怕，并合理地相信陌生人要杀他，且使用致命武力是唯一的自救方法，于是他拿出配枪，射杀了该陌生人。

该警官被控谋杀罪。在审判中，他声称自己是出于自卫。

该警官以自卫为由使用致命武力是否正当？
options:
A. No, because the officer was not defending his home and had an obligation to retreat or to repel with less than deadly force.
不成立，因为该警官并非在保卫其住所，且有义务先行退避或使用非致命武力进行反击。

B. No, because the stranger did not in fact intend to harm the officer and the officer was incorrect in believing that he did.
不成立，因为陌生人实际上无意伤害该警官，且警官的此项认知是错误的。

C. Yes, because the killing was in hot blood upon sufficient provocation.
成立，因为杀人行为是在充分挑衅下的一时激愤所致。

D. Yes, because the officer reasonably believed the stranger was planning to kill him and that deadly force was required.
成立，因为该警官合理地相信陌生人正图谋杀他，且使用致命武力是必要的。
data.explanation:
The use of deadly force in self-defense is justified and a defense to murder - an unlawful killing of another with malice aforethought (eg, intent to inflict serious bodily harm) - when the defendant:
  • actually and reasonably believed that deadly force was necessary to prevent imminent serious bodily harm or death and
  • was not the initial aggressor - ie, did not engage in physical force first or intentionally provoke the altercation.
Here, the officer intentionally shot and killed the stranger. But the officer actually and reasonably believed that deadly force was necessary to prevent his imminent death because the stranger had pulled out a knife and threatened to kill the officer. And since the officer was not the initial aggressor, he justifiably used deadly force in self-defense.

(Choice A) In most jurisdictions, a person has no duty to retreat or repel an attack before using deadly force in self-defense - even when the person is outside his/her home (as seen here). But in a minority of jurisdictions, a person who is outside his/her home must retreat before using deadly force if he/she can safely do so.

(Choice B) To use deadly force in self-defense, the person's actual belief that serious bodily harm or death is imminent need only be reasonable - not correct. Therefore, the officer's incorrect belief that the stranger intended to harm him does not negate this defense.

(Choice C) Proof that the defendant intentionally killed in hot blood upon sufficient provocation - ie, an action that would cause a reasonable person to lose control - reduces murder to voluntary manslaughter. But it does not justify the use of deadly force in self-defense.

Educational objective: A defendant may justifiably use deadly force in self-defense when he/she (1) actually and reasonably believes that deadly force is necessary to prevent serious bodily harm or death and (2) is not the initial aggressor.



选项正确率统计：A选项 2%，B选项 1%，C选项 0%，D选项 94%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

在被告符合以下条件时，为自卫而使用致命武力是正当的，并可作为对谋杀罪的抗辩——谋杀罪是指怀有预谋恶意（例如，意图造成严重身体伤害）而非法杀害他人：
  • 实际上且合理地相信，使用致命武力对于防止迫在眉睫的严重身体伤害或死亡是必要的，并且
  • 不是最初的攻击者——即，没有首先使用物理暴力或故意挑起争端。
在本案中，警官故意开枪射杀了陌生人。但警官实际上且合理地相信，使用致命武力对于防止自己即将面临的死亡是必要的，因为陌生人拔出刀并威胁要杀死他。而且，由于警官不是最初的攻击者，他以自卫为由使用致命武力是正当的。

(选项A) 在大多数司法管辖区，个人在为自卫而使用致命武力前，没有退避或击退攻击的义务——即使此人身处其住所之外（如本案所示）。但在少数司法管辖区，当事人若身处其住所之外，且可以安全退避时，必须在采取致命武力前先行退避。

(选项B) 为了以自卫目的使用致命武力，当事人对于严重身体伤害或死亡迫在眉睫的实际信念，仅需合理即可，而无需正确。因此，该警官关于陌生人意图伤害他的错误信念，并不会使该自卫抗辩无效。

(选项C) 证明被告是在充分挑衅下因一时激愤而故意杀人——即，某种足以使一个理性人失控的行为——这会将谋杀罪降格为任意过失杀人罪（voluntary manslaughter）。但这并不能证明以自卫为由使用致命武力是正当的。

教学目标：被告在以下情况下可以正当地使用致命武力进行自卫：（1）他/她实际上且合理地相信，使用致命武力对于防止严重的身体伤害或死亡是必要的；以及（2）他/她不是最初的攻击者。

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

刑法：自卫与致命武力
(Self-Defense & Deadly Force)

⚖️ 核心法则 (The Rule)

一个人在以下情况下有权使用致命武力 (Deadly Force) 进行自卫：

  1. 非挑衅者 (Without Fault)： 他不是最初的攻击者。
  2. 迫在眉睫 (Imminent)： 他面临迫在眉睫的非法攻击。
  3. 合理信念 (Reasonable Belief)： 他实际上且合理地相信，使用致命武力对于防止死亡或严重身体伤害 (Death or Great Bodily Harm) 是必要的。
🔍 关键考点：合理信念 (Reasonable Belief)

本题的核心在于区分客观事实 (Objective Reality) 与主观合理信念 (Subjective Reasonable Belief)。

🧠
信念无需正确，只需合理
(Belief need not be correct, only reasonable)
即使攻击者实际上是在开玩笑或拿着假枪，只要受害人在当时的情境下，合理地认为威胁是真实的，自卫就是正当的。
🔪
本案应用
陌生人拿出了刀，大声辱骂，并明确威胁要杀人。任何理性的警官（或普通人）在此时都会相信生命受到威胁。因此，尽管陌生人内心并不想杀人，但这不影响警官自卫的正当性。
✅ 正确答案：D

成立，因为该警官合理地相信陌生人正图谋杀他，且使用致命武力是必要的。

这直接对应了自卫的核心要素：基于合理信念 (Reasonable Belief) 的必要性。警官的反应符合理性人标准，因此构成正当防卫 (Justification)，完全免除刑事责任。

❌ 为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 A (退避义务 Duty to Retreat)：
错误。 1. 多数规则 (Majority Rule)：大多数州不要求退避，允许“坚守阵地” (Stand Your Ground)。 2. 必要性：题目中警官认为开枪是“唯一的自救方法” (only salvation)，暗示无法安全退避。
选项 B (实际意图 Actual Intent)：
错误。 自卫权取决于表象 (Appearances) 而非攻击者的内心秘密意图。如果必须等确认对方真的想杀人才能反击，自卫权将形同虚设。
选项 C (激愤/挑衅 Hot Blood/Provocation)：
错误。 “激愤”通常用于将谋杀罪 (Murder) 降格为故意非预谋杀人罪 (Voluntary Manslaughter)，这是一种减轻情节 (Mitigation)，而不是正当化事由 (Justification)。自卫会导致无罪释放，而激愤仍会定罪。
💡 MBE 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)

当题目中出现“实际上没有意图伤害”或“假枪”的情节时，考官通常在测试你对“合理信念” (Reasonable Belief) 的掌握。切记：刑法看重的是被告人视角下的合理性，而不是上帝视角下的事实真相。

© MBE Study Guide | Criminal Law

questions.question:
A woman and her friend were engaged in a heated discussion over the relative merits of their favorite professional football teams when the woman said, "You have to be one of the dumbest persons around." The friend punched the woman in the face. The woman then drew a knife and stabbed her friend in the stomach. Other persons then stepped in and stopped any further fighting. Despite the pleas of the other persons, the friend refused to go to a hospital or to seek medical treatment. About two hours later, he died as the result of a loss of blood.
The woman was charged with murder. At trial, medical evidence established that if the friend had been taken to a hospital, he would have survived. At the end of the case, the woman moves for a judgment of acquittal or, in the alternative, for an instruction on the elements of voluntary manslaughter.
How should the court rule on the woman's motions?

choices.a: Deny both motions.
choices.b: Deny the motion for acquittal, but instruct on manslaughter because the woman acted with criminal negligence.
choices.c: Deny the motion for acquittal, but instruct on manslaughter because there is evidence of adequate provocation.
choices.d: Grant the motion for acquittal.

data.questionStem:
Q85107

A woman and her friend were engaged in a heated discussion over the relative merits of their favorite professional football teams when the woman said, "You have to be one of the dumbest persons around." The friend punched the woman in the face. The woman then drew a knife and stabbed her friend in the stomach. Other persons then stepped in and stopped any further fighting. Despite the pleas of the other persons, the friend refused to go to a hospital or to seek medical treatment. About two hours later, he died as the result of a loss of blood.

The woman was charged with murder. At trial, medical evidence established that if the friend had been taken to a hospital, he would have survived. At the end of the case, the woman moves for a judgment of acquittal or, in the alternative, for an instruction on the elements of voluntary manslaughter.

How should the court rule on the woman's motions?

一名女子和她的朋友正在就他们各自最喜爱的职业橄榄球队的优劣进行激烈讨论，这时女子说：“你真是周围最蠢的人之一。”朋友一拳打在女子的脸上。该女子随后拔刀刺向朋友的腹部。其他人随后介入，制止了进一步的打斗。尽管其他人恳求，该朋友仍拒绝前往医院或寻求医疗救治。大约两小时后，他因失血过多而死亡。

该女子被控谋杀罪。在审判中，医学证据表明，如果该朋友被送往医院，他本可以存活。在案件审理结束时，该女子请求作出无罪判决，或者，作为替代方案，请求法庭就自愿过失杀人罪（voluntary manslaughter）的构成要件进行指示。

法院应如何裁定该女子的请求？
options:
A. Deny both motions.
驳回两项请求。

B. Deny the motion for acquittal, but instruct on manslaughter because the woman acted with criminal negligence.
驳回无罪判决的请求，但就过失杀人罪进行指示，因为该女子是基于刑事过失（criminal negligence）行事。

C. Deny the motion for acquittal, but instruct on manslaughter because there is evidence of adequate provocation.
驳回无罪判决的请求，但就过失杀人罪进行指示，因为有充分挑衅（adequate provocation）的证据。

D. Grant the motion for acquittal.
批准无罪判决的请求。
data.explanation:
A motion for acquittal should be granted if there is insufficient evidence to support any element of the charged crime. Murder requires evidence that the defendant acted with malice aforethought and caused the unlawful killing of another. Causation must be both:

  • actual - (1) the unlawful result would not have occurred but for the defendant's conduct or (2) when multiple causes exist, the defendant's conduct was a substantial factor in causing that result and
  • proximate - the unlawful result was a foreseeable consequence of the defendant's actions.


An intervening cause - ie, an event that happens after the defendant acts but before harm occurs - will break the chain of proximate causation if the event was unforeseeable.

Here, the woman actually and proximately caused her friend to die by stabbing him with malice aforethought. And though the friend's refusal to seek medical treatment is an intervening cause - and the friend would have survived had he gone to the hospital - that refusal was foreseeable . Therefore, it did not negate proximate causation and the motion for acquittal should be denied (Choice D).

However, the court should instruct the jury on voluntary manslaughter if a reasonable jury could find that the defendant intentionally killed the victim:

  • in response to adequate provocation - an act that would cause sudden and intense passion in a reasonable person - and
  • in the heat of passion - before a reasonable person could, and the defendant did, cool off from the provocation.


Here, the woman intentionally stabbed the friend while impassioned by his punch. And since a reasonable jury could find that the punch was adequate provocation, the court should give an instruction on voluntary manslaughter (Choice A).

(Choice B) Murder can be mitigated to involuntary manslaughter if the defendant acted with criminal negligence. But here, the woman acted with

malice aforethought - not mere criminal negligence - when she intentionally stabbed the friend. Therefore, an involuntary-manslaughter instruction is inappropriate.

Educational objective: Murder requires proof of actual (but for) and proximate (foreseeable) causation. An unforeseeable intervening cause eliminates proximate causation, but a foreseeable intervening cause (eg, a victim's refusal to seek medical treatment) does not.



选项正确率统计：A选项 34%，B选项 12%，C选项 45%（正确选项），D选项 7%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

如果没有足够的证据支持被控罪行的任何一项构成要件，则应批准无罪判决的请求。谋杀罪要求有证据证明被告人怀有预谋恶意（malice aforethought）并造成他人非法死亡。因果关系（Causation）必须同时满足：

  • 事实上的因果关系（actual causation）- (1) 若无（but for）被告人的行为，非法结果便不会发生 或 (2) 当存在多重原因时，被告人的行为是导致该结果的实质性因素 并且
  • 法律上的因果关系（proximate causation）- 非法结果是被告人行为的可预见后果。


如果介入原因（intervening cause）——即在被告人行为之后、损害发生之前发生的事件——是不可预见的，则会切断法律上因果关系（proximate causation）的链条。

在本案中，该女子怀有预谋恶意（malice aforethought）刺伤朋友的行为，在事实上和法律上都导致了其朋友的死亡。尽管朋友拒绝寻求医疗救治是一个介入原因——并且如果他去了医院本可以存活——但这种拒绝是可预见的。因此，这并未否定法律上的因果关系，故无罪判决的请求应被驳回（选项D）。

然而，如果一个理性的陪审团能够认定被告人故意杀死受害人，且符合以下条件，法院应就自愿过失杀人罪（voluntary manslaughter）对陪审团进行指示：

  • 为回应充分挑衅（adequate provocation）——一种会引起理性之人突发和强烈情绪的行为—— 并且
  • 处于激情之中（in the heat of passion）——在一个理性的人能够冷静下来之前，且被告人也确实未能从挑衅中冷静下来。


在本案中，女子因朋友的拳击而情绪激动，并在此期间故意刺伤了他。并且，由于一个理性的陪审团可以认定该拳击构成了充分挑衅，法院应就自愿过失杀人罪（voluntary manslaughter）作出指示（选项A）。

（选项B）如果被告人是基于刑事过失（criminal negligence）行事，谋杀罪可被减轻为非自愿过失杀人罪（involuntary manslaughter）。但在本案中，当女子故意刺伤朋友时，其行为是怀有

预谋恶意（malice aforethought）的——而不仅仅是刑事过失（criminal negligence）。因此，就不非自愿过失杀人罪（involuntary manslaughter）进行指示是不恰当的。

教学目标：谋杀罪需要证明事实上的因果关系（即“若无”则不发生）和法律上的因果关系（即可预见性）。一个不可预见的介入原因会排除法律上的因果关系，但一个可预见的介入原因（例如，受害人拒绝寻求医疗救治）则不会。

MBE 刑法考点解析

因果关系与激情杀人

✅ 正确答案：C

法院应驳回无罪判决的请求，但必须向陪审团提供关于自愿过失杀人罪 (Voluntary Manslaughter) 的指示。

⚖️ 考点一：因果关系 (Causation)

问题核心：受害人拒绝就医导致死亡，被告是否可以免责？

在刑法中，被告要对结果负责，必须同时满足：

  • 事实因果关系 (Actual Cause): "But for" test。如果被告没刺那一刀，受害人不会死。
  • 法律因果关系 (Proximate Cause): 结果必须是可预见的 (Foreseeable)。

关键规则：受害人拒绝医疗救治属于介入原因 (Intervening Cause)。但是，除非受害人的行为极其反常，否则拒绝就医通常被视为可预见的 (Foreseeable)。

👉 本案分析：虽然受害人如果不拒绝就医就能活下来，但被告刺伤受害人是导致死亡的实质原因。受害人固执不就医并未切断因果链条。因此，证据足以支持谋杀指控，不能直接判无罪 (Acquittal)。

🔥 考点二：自愿过失杀人 (Voluntary Manslaughter)

问题核心：是否应给陪审团“激情杀人”的选项？

如果谋杀是在“激情状态”下实施的，可以减轻为自愿过失杀人。这需要满足：

  • 充分挑衅 (Adequate Provocation): 能够让一个理性的人失去自控。
  • 激情之中 (Heat of Passion): 被告确实被激怒了。
  • 未冷静 (No Cooling Off): 挑衅和杀害之间没有足够的时间冷静。

👉 本案分析：受害人先动手打了被告一拳 (Battery)。在普通法中，殴打 (Battery) 通常被视为足以构成“充分挑衅”的证据。被告随即反击，处于激情状态中。

因此，这是一个事实问题，必须交给陪审团决定，法官应给予相应的法律指示。

❌ 为什么排除其他选项？

  • 选项 A (全部驳回): 错误。因为存在“充分挑衅”的证据，法官必须允许陪审团考虑过失杀人的可能性。
  • 选项 B (刑事过失): 错误。被告是故意刺伤受害人，而非疏忽大意。刑事过失 (Criminal Negligence) 通常对应非自愿过失杀人 (Involuntary Manslaughter)，与本案“拔刀刺腹”的故意行为不符。
  • 选项 D (直接无罪): 错误。如前所述，受害人拒绝就医不能切断因果关系，被告仍需对死亡负责。

💡 MBE 考试技巧

1. 区分“定罪”与“指示”：
题目问的是“法院应如何处理动议”。对于无罪判决 (Acquittal)，标准是“没有任何理性陪审团能定罪”；对于法律指示 (Instruction)，标准是“只要有证据支持该理论”。门槛不同。

2. 介入原因的判断：
记住：受害人的疏忽（如拒绝治疗、伤口感染）通常不会切断被告的责任。只有不可预见的重大巧合（如救护车被陨石击中）才会切断因果链。

questions.question:
After being fired from his job, a financial analyst drank almost a quart of vodka and decided to ride the bus home. While on the bus, he saw a briefcase he mistakenly thought was his own and began struggling with the passenger carrying the briefcase. The analyst knocked the passenger to the floor, took the briefcase, and fled. The analyst was arrested and charged with robbery.
Should he be convicted of robbery?

choices.a: No, because he used no threats and was intoxicated.
choices.b: No, because his mistake negated the required specific intent.
choices.c: Yes, because his intoxication was voluntary.
choices.d: Yes, because mistake is no defense to robbery.

data.questionStem:
Q85123

After being fired from his job, a financial analyst drank almost a quart of vodka and decided to ride the bus home. While on the bus, he saw a briefcase he mistakenly thought was his own and began struggling with the passenger carrying the briefcase. The analyst knocked the passenger to the floor, took the briefcase, and fled. The analyst was arrested and charged with robbery.

Should he be convicted of robbery?

一名金融分析师在被解雇后，喝了将近一夸脱的伏特加，并决定乘坐公交车回家。在公交车上，他看到了一个他误以为是自己的公文包，并开始与携带该公文包的乘客发生争抢。该分析师将乘客撞倒在地，拿走了公文包，然后逃离。该分析师被逮捕并被指控犯有抢劫罪(robbery)。

他是否应被判犯有抢劫罪(robbery)？
options:
A. No, because he used no threats and was intoxicated.
不应，因为他没有使用威胁且处于醉酒状态。

B. No, because his mistake negated the required specific intent.
不应，因为他的错误否定了所要求的特定意图(specific intent)。

C. Yes, because his intoxication was voluntary.
应，因为他的醉酒是自愿的。

D. Yes, because mistake is no defense to robbery.
应，因为事实错误(mistake)不能作为抢劫罪(robbery)的辩护理由。
data.explanation:
Robbery requires proof of the following elements:
  • The defendant unlawfully took and carried away the victim's property.
  • The property was taken from the victim's person or presence by force or threat of force (Choice A).
  • The defendant specifically intended to permanently deprive the victim of the property (ie, intent to steal).


Mistake of fact is a defense to robbery (and other specific intent crimes) when the defendant's honest but mistaken belief negates the requisite intent (Choice D). This is true even when that mistake is unreasonable.

Here, the analyst took the passenger's briefcase by force when he knocked the passenger to the floor and fled with it. But the analyst did not intend to deprive the passenger of his briefcase since the analyst honestly but mistakenly believed that he owned it. And though that mistaken belief likely was unreasonable (and the result of the analyst's intoxication), it still negated the specific intent required for robbery. Therefore, the analyst should be acquitted.

(Choice C) Voluntary intoxication is a defense to specific intent crimes if it prevented the defendant from forming the requisite intent. And since the analyst's intoxication may have contributed to his mistaken belief that he owned the briefcase, it would support an acquittal - not a conviction.

Educational objective: Mistake of fact is a defense to specific intent crimes (eg, robbery) when the defendant's honest but mistaken belief negates the requisite intent - even if that belief was unreasonable.



选项正确率统计：A选项 4%，B选项 85%（正确选项），C选项 7%，D选项 2%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

抢劫罪 (Robbery) 的定罪需要证明以下要素：
  • 被告非法取得并带走了受害人的财产。
  • 该财产是通过暴力或暴力威胁从受害人的人身或其在场范围内夺走的 (选项 A)。
  • 被告具有永久剥夺受害人财产的特定意图 (specifically intended)（即盗窃意图）。


事实错误 (Mistake of fact) 在被告诚实但错误的认知否定了必要意图的情况下，可以作为抢劫罪 (robbery)（以及其他特定意图犯罪）的辩护理由 (选项 D)。即使该错误是不合理的，这一点也成立。

在本案中，分析师将乘客撞倒在地并携公文包逃离，这是通过暴力获取了乘客的公文包。但是，该分析师并无意图剥夺乘客的公文包，因为他诚实地误认为自己是该公文包的所有者。而且，尽管这种错误的认知可能是不合理的（并且是分析师醉酒的结果），它仍然否定了抢劫罪所要求的特定意图。因此，该分析师应被宣告无罪。

(选项 C) 如果自愿醉酒 (Voluntary intoxication) 妨碍了被告形成必要的意图，那么它可以作为特定意图犯罪的辩护理由。并且，由于分析师的醉酒状态可能导致他误认为自己拥有该公文包，这将支持无罪裁定，而非定罪。

教学目标：当被告诚实但错误的认知否定了必要的意图时，事实错误 (Mistake of fact) 可以作为特定意图犯罪（例如，抢劫罪 robbery）的辩护理由——即使该认知是不合理的。

MBE 刑法考点解析

Robbery & Specific Intent Defenses
正确答案：选项 B 不应定罪，因为他的错误否定了所要求的特定意图 (Specific Intent)。
核心考点：特定意图 (Specific Intent)

抢劫罪 (Robbery) 是严重的盗窃罪 (Aggravated Larceny)。要构成抢劫罪，检方必须证明被告具有“永久剥夺他人财产的意图” (Intent to permanently deprive)。

这属于刑法中的特定意图 (Specific Intent)。

事实错误 (Mistake of Fact) 的抗辩

在 MBE 考试中，针对特定意图犯罪的抗辩规则非常明确：

  • 如果被告存在诚实的 (Honest) 事实错误；
  • 即使这个错误是不合理的 (Unreasonable)；
  • 只要该错误导致被告无法形成犯罪所需的“特定意图”，被告即无罪。

本案应用：
被告喝醉了，诚实地（虽然很不合理地）认为公文包是自己的。如果你认为某物是你自己的，你就不可能有“偷窃”他人物品的意图。因此，抢劫罪的核心要素缺失。

为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 A 错误 理由： 抢劫罪的要素是使用暴力 (Force) 或 威胁 (Threats)。题目中被告将乘客“撞倒在地”，这已经构成了暴力 (Force)。因此，“没有使用威胁”不能作为辩护理由。
选项 C 错误 理由： 虽然醉酒是自愿的 (Voluntary Intoxication)，但在普通法中，自愿醉酒可以作为特定意图犯罪的辩护理由（如果醉酒程度严重到无法形成意图）。选项 C 声称因为醉酒是自愿的所以“应定罪”，这与法律原则相反。
选项 D 错误 理由： 这是一个常见的陷阱。事实错误 (Mistake of Fact) 是抢劫罪的有效辩护理由，因为它否定了特定意图。只有在“一般意图犯罪” (General Intent Crimes，如殴打罪 Battery) 中，不合理的错误才不能作为辩护。
🎓 MBE 抢分技巧：

遇到涉及“错误” (Mistake) 或 “醉酒” (Intoxication) 的题目时，第一步永远是判断该罪行是特定意图 (Specific Intent) 还是一般意图 (General Intent)。

  • 特定意图 (如 Robbery, Burglary, Larceny)： 任何诚实的错误（无论是否合理）都是辩护理由；自愿醉酒也是辩护理由。
  • 一般意图 (如 Battery, Rape)： 只有合理的错误才是辩护理由；自愿醉酒通常不是辩护理由。

questions.question:
A man was charged with violating a state statute making it a crime "to hold or promote an illegal gambling event." The statutory definition of illegal gambling event includes "any private gathering held for the purpose of gambling in which the host charges an entrance fee or takes a percentage of the wagered money or players' winnings." At trial, it was established that the man arranged and hosted a private high-stakes poker tournament at his large estate and, in violation of the statute, took a $10,000 entrance fee from each player.
Which of the following facts, if proved at trial, would serve as the man's best defense?

choices.a: At the time of trial, the statute making the man's conduct illegal was being challenged in the state's highest court.
choices.b: The man had just moved to the state and was unaware that his conduct was illegal.
choices.c: The man relied on the advice of his attorney, who erroneously told the man that his conduct was legal.
choices.d: The statute making the man's conduct illegal was not reasonably made available prior to the conduct.

data.questionStem:
Q85132

A man was charged with violating a state statute making it a crime "to hold or promote an illegal gambling event." The statutory definition of illegal gambling event includes "any private gathering held for the purpose of gambling in which the host charges an entrance fee or takes a percentage of the wagered money or players' winnings." At trial, it was established that the man arranged and hosted a private high-stakes poker tournament at his large estate and, in violation of the statute, took a $10,000 entrance fee from each player.

Which of the following facts, if proved at trial, would serve as the man's best defense?

一名男子被指控违反了一项州法律，该法律将“举办或推广非法赌博活动”定为犯罪。非法赌博活动的法定定义包括“为赌博目的而举行的任何私人聚会，且主办方收取入场费或从赌注或玩家的奖金中抽取一定比例的金额。”审判中，事实表明该男子在其大型庄园内组织并主办了一场私人高额扑克锦标赛，并且违反了该法律，向每位玩家收取了10,000美元的入场费。

以下哪项事实，如果在审判中得以证实，能成为该男子最好的抗辩理由？
options:
A. At the time of trial, the statute making the man's conduct illegal was being challenged in the state's highest court.
在审判时，将该男子行为定为非法的法律正在该州的最高法院受到挑战。

B. The man had just moved to the state and was unaware that his conduct was illegal.
该男子刚搬到这个州，并且不知道其行为是违法的。

C. The man relied on the advice of his attorney, who erroneously told the man that his conduct was legal.
该男子依赖其律师的建议，该律师错误地告知该男子其行为是合法的。

D. The statute making the man's conduct illegal was not reasonably made available prior to the conduct.
将该男子行为定为非法的法律，在其行为发生前未被合理地公布。
data.explanation:
Mistake of law v. Mistake of fact


DefinitionApplicability
Mistake of lawDefendant mistakenly believes conduct not prohibited by lawNo defense unless:
  • Law prohibiting conduct was unavailable
  • Defendant reasonably relied on invalid law
  • Mistake negates mens rea†
Mistake of factDefendant is mistaken as to a matter of factWhen mistake negates mens rea:
  • Specific intent - defense if honest mistake
  • General intent & malice - defense if honest & reasonable mistake
  • Strict liability - no defense
†Mens rea - state of mind necessary to be guilty of criminal offense

A defendant's mistaken belief that his/her conduct was not prohibited by law (ie, mistake of law ) is generally not a defense to criminal liability (Choice B). But mistake of law is a defense when:
  • the charged conduct is classified as a malum prohibitum offense - ie, an offense that is not inherently or obviously wrong (eg, gambling) and
  • the statute making the conduct illegal was not reasonably made available prior to the conduct.


Here, the man arranged and hosted a private high-stakes poker tournament and, in violation of the state statute, took a $10,000 entrance fee from each player. But if the man can establish that the statute making his conduct illegal was not reasonably made available prior to the tournament, he can rely on a mistake-of-law defense. That is because the charged offense is malum prohibitum (ie, not inherently wrong).

(Choice A) The fact that the statute making the man's conduct illegal was being challenged in the state's highest court at the time of the man's trial would not serve as a defense. A mere challenge to a statute does not invalidate it.

(Choice C) Erroneous legal advice from an attorney generally is not a valid defense, regardless of whether a reasonable person would have known that the advice was erroneous or relied on it. However, such advice may serve as a defense if it negates a mental state required by a statute - eg, a statute requiring that the defendant knowingly violate the law or act without legal privilege (not seen here).

Educational objective: Mistake of law is a defense to criminal liability when (1) the charged offense is classified as a malum prohibitum offense and (2) the statute making the defendant's conduct illegal was not reasonably made available prior to the conduct.

选项正确率统计：A选项 13%，B选项 2%，C选项 13%，D选项 70%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

法律错误与事实错误之比较


定义适用性
法律错误被告错误地认为其行为未被法律禁止不构成抗辩理由，除非：
  • 禁止该行为的法律未被公布
  • 被告合理地依赖了一项无效的法律
  • 该错误排除了犯罪意图(mens rea)†
事实错误被告对某一事实存在错误认识当该错误排除了犯罪意图时：
  • 特定意图犯罪 - 如果是真实错误，则构成抗辩理由
  • 一般意图犯罪与恶意犯罪 - 如果是真实且合理的错误，则构成抗辩理由
  • 严格责任犯罪 - 不构成抗辩理由
†Mens rea - 构成刑事犯罪所必需的心理状态

被告错误地认为其行为未被法律禁止（即，法律错误），通常不构成对刑事责任的抗辩理由（选项B）。但在以下情况下，法律错误是一种抗辩理由：
  • 被指控的行为被归类为 malum prohibitum（法定犯）——即，其本身并非固有或明显错误的犯罪行为（例如，赌博）并且
  • 将该行为定为非法的法律在该行为发生前未被合理地公布。


在本案中，该男子组织并主办了一场私人高额扑克锦标赛，并违反州法律向每位玩家收取了10,000美元的入场费。但如果该男子能够证明，将他行为定为非法的法律在锦标赛之前未被合理地公布，他就可以依赖法律错误的抗辩理由。这是因为被指控的罪行是 malum prohibitum（法定犯）（即，其本身并非固有错误）。

（选项A）在审判时，将该男子行为定为非法的法律正在该州最高法院受到挑战，这一事实不能作为抗辩理由。仅仅对一项法律提出挑战并不会使其失效。

（选项C）来自律师的错误法律建议通常不是一个有效的抗辩理由，无论一个理性人是否会知道该建议是错误的或是否会依赖它。然而，如果该建议排除了法律所要求的心理状态，则可以作为抗辩理由——例如，法律要求被告明知故犯地违反法律或在没有法律特权的情况下行事（本案中未见此种情况）。

教学目标：当（1）被指控的罪行被归类为 malum prohibitum（法定犯），以及（2）将被告行为定为非法的法律在该行为发生前未被合理地公布时，法律错误是刑事责任的抗辩理由。

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析：法律认识错误

本题考察刑法中的核心原则：法律认识错误 (Mistake of Law) 是否可以作为刑事抗辩理由。

核心原则：
通常情况下，"不知法不免责" (Ignorantia juris non excusat)。被告人不知道某种行为是违法的，通常不能作为抗辩理由。

为什么选项 D 是最佳抗辩？

虽然原则上不知法不免责，但在美国宪法正当程序条款 (Due Process Clause) 下，存在一个重要的例外，即 Lambert 例外 (源自 Lambert v. California)。

如果满足以下两个条件，法律认识错误可以作为抗辩：

  1. 该罪行属于 Malum Prohibitum (法定犯)：即行为本身并非本质邪恶（如杀人、强奸），只是因为法律禁止才违法（如赌博、未注册登记）。
  2. 该法律在行为发生前未被合理公布 (Not reasonably made available)，且被告人不知情。

在本题中：

  • 性质：举办扑克比赛属于 Malum Prohibitum（法定犯），不是天理难容的罪行。
  • 公布情况：选项 D 指出该法律未被合理公布。

因此，如果法律没有给公民提供“公平的告知” (Fair Notice)，且行为本身不具有明显的道德非难性，被告可以以此作为抗辩。

常见陷阱分析 (为什么其他选项错误)

🚫 选项 B (刚搬来不知情)：
这是最典型的干扰项。仅仅是“不知道法律” (Ignorance of the law) 永远不是抗辩理由，除非符合上述极少数例外。无论你是刚搬来还是住了很久，都有义务了解当地法律。
🚫 选项 C (依赖律师建议)：
依赖律师建议 (Reliance on Counsel) 通常不是抗辩理由。

例外情况仅限于： 1. 依赖的是官方解释（如法院判决、行政命令），而非私人律师。 2. 该建议否定了犯罪所需的特定心理状态 (Specific Intent)。但在本题这种一般意图犯罪中，律师说“没事”不能免责。

🚫 选项 A (法律正受挑战)：
法律在被法院正式废除之前，依然有效。仅仅有人在法院挑战该法律，并不赋予被告违反该法律的权利。

MBE 解题技巧

在处理 Mistake of Law 题目时，请遵循以下思维路径：

  1. 默认规则：首先假设“不知者不无罪”。
  2. 检查例外：
    • 是否依赖了官方（法官/官员）的错误解释？
    • 法律是否未公布且行为属于法定犯 (Regulatory offense)？
    • 法条本身是否要求“明知违法” (如税务欺诈中的 "Willfully")？
  3. 排除干扰：私人律师的建议、个人的善意误解、文化背景差异，通常都不构成抗辩。
MBE Criminal Law Review | Mistake of Law

questions.question:
During an altercation between a man and his coworker at a company picnic, the man suffered a knife wound in his abdomen and the coworker was charged with assault and attempted murder. At his trial, the coworker seeks to offer evidence that he had been drinking at the picnic and was highly intoxicated at the time of the altercation.
In a jurisdiction that follows the common-law rules concerning admissibility of evidence of intoxication, how should the court rule on evidence of the coworker's intoxication?

choices.a: Admit the evidence subject to an instruction that it pertains only to the assault charge.
choices.b: Admit the evidence subject to an instruction that it pertains only to the attempted-murder charge.
choices.c: Admit the evidence without limitation.
choices.d: Exclude the evidence altogether.

At his trial, the coworker seeks to offer evidence that he had been drinking at the picnic and was highly intoxicated at the time of the altercation.

In a jurisdiction that follows the common law rules concerning admissibility of evidence of intoxication, how should the court rule on evidence of the coworker's intoxication?

一名男子在公司野餐时与同事发生争执，腹部被刀刺伤，其同事被控攻击罪 (assault) 和谋杀未遂 (attempted murder)。在审判中，该同事试图提供证据，证明他在争执发生时一直在野餐会上饮酒，并处于高度醉酒状态。

在一个遵循关于醉酒证据可采性的普通法 (common law) 规则的司法管辖区，法院应如何就该同事的醉酒证据作出裁定？
options:
A. Admit the evidence subject to an instruction that it pertains only to the assault charge.
采纳该证据，但须附带指示，说明该证据仅与攻击罪 (assault) 指控相关。

B. Admit the evidence subject to an instruction that it pertains only to the attempted-murder charge.
采纳该证据，但须附带指示，说明该证据仅与谋杀未遂 (attempted-murder) 指控相关。

C. Admit the evidence without limitation.
不加限制地采纳该证据。

D. Exclude the evidence altogether.
完全排除该证据。
data.explanation:
Specific intent crimes


(criminal acts committed to purposely or knowingly cause a particular result)
  • A ssault
  • M urder requiring premeditation or deliberation
  • B urglary
  • I nchoate crimes - solicitation, conspiracy, attempt
  • T heft crimes - larceny, robbery, embezzlement, false pretenses, forgery, receiving stolen property, extortion


Mnemonic: AMBIT

Voluntary intoxication is the deliberate ingestion of a substance that the defendant knows, or should know, tends to have intoxicating effects. At common law (and in most jurisdictions), voluntary intoxication is a defense to specific intent crimes if it prevented the defendant from forming the required intent.

Here, the coworker is on trial for both:
  • assault - which requires proof that the defendant specifically intended to (1) commit battery or (2) place the victim in apprehension of imminent bodily harm and
  • attempted murder - which requires proof that the defendant specifically intended to kill the victim.


Since these are both specific intent crimes, the coworker may offer evidence of his voluntary intoxication to establish that the intoxication prevented him from forming the required intent for either charge. Therefore, the court should admit evidence of the coworker's intoxication without limitation (Choices A, B, & D).

Educational objective: When a defendant is charged with a specific intent crime, evidence of voluntary intoxication may be offered to show that the intoxication prevented him from forming the required intent.

选项正确率统计：A选项 10%，B选项 35%，C选项 45%（正确选项），D选项 8%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

特定意图犯罪 (Specific Intent Crimes)


(指为了故意或明知地造成特定结果而实施的犯罪行为)
  • Assault (攻击罪)
  • Murder (需要预谋或深思熟虑的谋杀罪)
  • Burglary (入室犯法罪)
  • Inchoate crimes (未遂罪) - solicitation (教唆), conspiracy (共谋), attempt (未遂)
  • Theft crimes (盗窃类犯罪) - larceny (普通盗窃罪), robbery (抢劫罪), embezzlement (侵占罪), false pretenses (诈骗罪), forgery (伪造罪), receiving stolen property (收受赃物罪), extortion (勒索罪)


助记词: AMBIT

自愿醉酒 (Voluntary intoxication) 是指被告明知或应知某种物质具有致醉效果而故意摄入。在普通法 (common law) 中（以及在大多数司法管辖区），如果自愿醉酒妨碍了被告形成必要的意图 (required intent)，则可作为对特定意图犯罪 (specific intent crimes) 的抗辩 (defense)。

在本案中，该同事因以下两项罪名受审：
  • Assault (攻击罪) - 要求证明被告具有特定意图去 (1) 实施 battery (伤害罪) 或 (2) 使受害人担忧即将发生的身体伤害 以及
  • Attempted murder (谋杀未遂) - 要求证明被告具有特定意图去杀害受害人。


由于这两项都是特定意图犯罪，该同事可以提供其自愿醉酒的证据，以证明醉酒状态妨碍了他形成任何一项指控所需的意图。因此，法院应不加限制地采纳该同事的醉酒证据（因此选项A、B和D是错误的）。

教学目的：当被告被控以特定意图犯罪时，可以提供自愿醉酒的证据，以证明醉酒状态妨碍了其形成必要的意图。

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law: Intoxication Defense
正确答案：选项 C
不加限制地采纳该证据 (Admit the evidence without limitation)。
核心法律规则

本题考察的是自愿醉酒 (Voluntary Intoxication) 对刑事责任的影响。在普通法 (Common Law) 规则下，判断醉酒证据是否可采的关键在于区分犯罪类型：

1. 特定意图犯罪 (Specific Intent Crimes)：
自愿醉酒可以作为抗辩理由。如果醉酒程度严重到被告无法形成特定的犯罪意图，则不能被定罪。
2. 一般意图犯罪 (General Intent Crimes)：
自愿醉酒不能作为抗辩理由。法律拟制认为，自愿摄入致醉物质本身就满足了 reckless (鲁莽) 或 general intent 的心理状态要求。
案情具体分析

本案中，被告面临两项指控，我们需要逐一分析它们属于哪类犯罪：

1. 谋杀未遂 (Attempted Murder)
Classification: Specific Intent

所有的“未遂罪” (Attempt) 都是特定意图犯罪。因为未遂要求被告具有实施目标犯罪的具体意图 (Specific Intent)。因此，醉酒证据可用于否定该意图。

2. 攻击罪 (Assault)
Classification: Specific Intent (Common Law)

在 MBE 考试的普通法规则中，Assault 通常被定义为：

  • Attempted Battery (伤害未遂)：需要实施伤害的特定意图。
  • Creation of Apprehension (制造恐慌)：需要故意使受害人产生恐惧的特定意图。

因此，Assault 在此处也被视为特定意图犯罪，醉酒证据同样适用。

MBE 必背口诀：AMBIT
特定意图犯罪 (Specific Intent Crimes)
A - Assault (攻击)
M - Murder (Premeditated 1st Degree) (一级谋杀)
B - Burglary (入室盗窃)
I - Inchoate Crimes (未遂、共谋、教唆)
T - Theft Crimes (所有盗窃类犯罪)
结论与解题技巧

由于本案中的两项指控（Assault 和 Attempted Murder）均属于 Specific Intent Crimes，被告的醉酒证据对于否定这两项罪名的心理状态 (Mens Rea) 都是相关的。

因此，法院应不加限制地 (without limitation) 采纳该证据，允许陪审团考虑醉酒是否导致被告无法形成这两项罪名所需的意图。

为什么排除其他选项？
  • 选项 A & B 错： 既然两项罪名都是特定意图犯罪，就没有理由限制证据只针对其中一项。
  • 选项 D 错： 只有当指控是“一般意图犯罪”（如 Battery, Rape, False Imprisonment）时，才应排除自愿醉酒的证据。

questions.question:
A woman was walking her dog one evening when she saw a strange man walking toward her neighbor's house holding a suspicious-looking tool. She decided to walk her dog past the side of the house to get a better view of the man. When she got closer, she noticed that he was using the tool to pry open a window. The woman also noticed that the man had an empty bag on the ground next to him. When the man managed to pry the window open, he grabbed the empty bag and began to climb inside. The woman ran toward the man, grabbed one of his shoes, and began hitting him until he fell back on the ground.
Given these facts, can the woman properly be convicted of criminal battery?

choices.a: No, because the woman acted justifiably.
choices.b: No, because the woman may use any amount of force to prevent a crime.
choices.c: Yes, because the woman had the requisite general intent for battery.
choices.d: Yes, because the woman was not the owner of the house.

data.questionStem:
Q85130

A woman was walking her dog one evening when she saw a strange man walking toward her neighbor's house holding a suspicious-looking tool. She decided to walk her dog past the side of the house to get a better view of the man. When she got closer, she noticed that he was using the tool to pry open a window. The woman also noticed that the man had an empty bag on the ground next to him. When the man managed to pry the window open, he grabbed the empty bag and began to climb inside. The woman ran toward the man, grabbed one of his shoes, and began hitting him until he fell back on the ground.

Given these facts, can the woman properly be convicted of criminal battery?

一名女子一天晚上遛狗时，看到一个陌生男子拿着一个可疑的工具走向她邻居的房子。她决定带着狗从房子侧面走过，以便更清楚地看到该男子。当她走近时，她注意到他正在用那个工具撬开一扇窗户。该女子还注意到该男子身旁的地上有一个空袋子。当该男子成功撬开窗户后，他抓起空袋子，开始往里爬。该女子跑向该男子，抓住他的一只鞋子，开始打他，直到他摔倒在地。

根据这些事实，该女子是否可以被正式定罪为刑事伤害罪？
options:
A. No, because the woman acted justifiably.
不可以，因为该女子的行为具有正当性。

B. No, because the woman may use any amount of force to prevent a crime.
不可以，因为该女子可以使用任何程度的武力来阻止犯罪。

C. Yes, because the woman had the requisite general intent for battery.
可以，因为该女子具备伤害罪所需的一般意图。

D. Yes, because the woman was not the owner of the house.
可以，因为该女子不是该房屋的所有人。
data.explanation:
Criminal battery is the unlawful application of force to another that causes bodily harm or offensive contact. However, a defendant's otherwise unlawful use of force may be justifiable if it is deemed socially acceptable due to the circumstances in which it occurred. For example, a person may use force to prevent a crime, but the level of force permitted depends on the seriousness of the crime:
  • Deadly force may be used to prevent the commission of a serious felony involving imminent death or serious bodily harm.
  • Nondeadly force may be used to prevent the commission of a lesser felony (here, burglary) or a breach-of-the-peace misdemeanor.


Here, the woman committed a battery when she grabbed the man's shoe and hit him. However, she only hit the man because she saw that he was trying to break into her neighbor's home. And since she applied only nondeadly force to prevent this felony, she acted justifiably and cannot properly be convicted of criminal battery.

(Choice B) The use of deadly force is justified only when the defendant actually and reasonably believes that such force is necessary to prevent imminent death or serious bodily harm to him/herself or others. Here, there is no indication that the man presented such a threat, so only nondeadly force could be used to stop him.

(Choice C) Criminal battery is a general intent crime because it requires that the criminal act be consciously performed (or criminally negligent). Here, although the woman acted with the requisite intent (by consciously grabbing and hitting the man), this does not impact her "crime prevention" defense.

(Choice D) For the "crime prevention" defense to apply, the crime being prevented need not be directed against the person, habitation, or property of the defendant; it may be directed against a third person or his/her property (here, the neighbor's house).

Educational objective: A person may use deadly force to prevent the commission of a serious felony involving imminent death or serious bodily harm. But only nondeadly force may be used to stop a lesser felony or a breach-of-the-peace misdemeanor.

选项正确率统计：A选项 62%（正确选项），B选项 4%，C选项 21%，D选项 10%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

刑事伤害罪（Criminal battery）是指对他人非法使用武力，造成身体伤害或冒犯性接触。然而，如果被告人非法使用武力的行为因其发生的情境而被认为在社会上是可接受的，则该行为可能具有正当性。例如，一个人可以使用武力来阻止犯罪，但所允许的武力程度取决于犯罪的严重性：
  • 致命性武力可用于阻止涉及迫在眉睫的死亡或严重身体伤害的严重重罪的实施。
  • 非致命性武力可用于阻止较轻的重罪（此处为入室犯法罪）或扰乱治安的轻罪的实施。


在本案中，该女子抓住该男子的鞋子并击打他时，构成了伤害罪。然而，她击打该男子仅仅是因为她看到他试图闯入她邻居的家。而且，由于她仅使用了非致命性武力来阻止这一重罪，她的行为具有正当性，不能被正式定罪为刑事伤害罪。

(选项B) 只有当被告人实际且合理地相信，为防止自己或他人遭受迫在眉睫的死亡或严重身体伤害，使用致命性武力是必要的，该行为才具有正当性。在本案中，没有迹象表明该男子构成了此类威胁，因此只能使用非致命性武力来阻止他。

(选项C) 刑事伤害罪是一种一般意图犯罪，因为它要求犯罪行为是有意识地实施（或构成刑事过失）的。在本案中，尽管该女子的行为具备了必要的意图（通过有意识地抓住并击打该男子），但这并不影响她的“阻止犯罪”的辩护理由。

(选项D) 为适用“阻止犯罪”的辩护理由，被阻止的犯罪无需针对被告人的人身、住所或财产；它可以是针对第三方或其财产（此处为邻居的房屋）。

教学目的： 一个人可以使用致命性武力来阻止涉及迫在眉睫的死亡或严重身体伤害的严重重罪的实施。但只能使用非致命性武力来阻止较轻的重罪或扰乱治安的轻罪。

References

Wayne R. LaFave, 2 Substantive Criminal Law § 10.7(c) (3d ed. 2020) (discussing the privilege to use force to prevent the commission of a felony or breach-of-the-peace misdemeanor).
