MBE 刑法考点解析

General Principles & Homicide

正确答案：选项 B
核心考点：预谋恶意 (Malice Aforethought)

在普通法 (Common Law) 中，谋杀罪 (Murder) 不仅仅指“故意杀人”。只要具备以下四种心态之一，即视为具有“预谋恶意”：

  1. 杀人意图 (Intent to kill)
  2. 造成严重身体伤害的意图 (Intent to inflict serious bodily injury)
  3. 极度鲁莽/堕落之心 (Depraved heart / Reckless indifference to human life)
  4. 重罪谋杀 (Felony murder)
为什么选 B？

题目要求找出被告无意造成死亡（法规旨在防止的损害），但仍最可能被定罪的情况。

在选项 B 中：

  • 行为：被告用棒球棒击打受害人面部。
  • 意图：意图造成严重伤害 (Intent to inflict serious injury)。
  • 结果：受害人死亡。

法律逻辑：虽然被告没有“杀人意图”，但他有“造成严重身体伤害的意图”。根据普通法，这满足了谋杀罪所需的 Mens Rea（犯罪心态），即预谋恶意 (Malice Aforethought)。因此，即使他不想让人死，他仍构成谋杀罪。

其他选项为何错误？
选项 A (纵火 Arson)：
纵火罪是针对财产的犯罪，要求有恶意 (Malice)，即故意或鲁莽 (Reckless) 地焚烧。被告只是想让警报短路，虽然导致了火灾，但这通常被视为疏忽 (Negligence)，很难证明他对“烧毁建筑”这一结果具有鲁莽的恶意。
选项 C (非自愿过失杀人 Involuntary Manslaughter)：
这通常需要“刑事疏忽” (Criminal Negligence)。虽然放假蛇是恶作剧，但在一般情况下，很难预见到这会导致心脏病发作死亡。这种行为通常不构成对人命安全标准的“严重偏离” (Gross deviation)。
选项 D (未遂 Attempt)：高频陷阱！
未遂罪 (Attempt) 总是属于“特殊意图犯罪” (Specific Intent Crime)。
即使目标罪行（如销售掺假药品）是严格责任 (Strict Liability) 犯罪，不需要意图；但要被判“未遂”，被告必须具有实施该犯罪的具体意图。既然总裁不知道药片有毒，他就没有“引入掺假药品”的具体意图，因此不能判未遂。
💡 MBE 备考锦囊：
遇到“谋杀”题，切记不要只寻找“杀人意图”。如果题目中出现了“意图造成严重身体伤害” (Intent to inflict SBI) 且导致了死亡，这在 MBE 考试中几乎总是构成谋杀罪 (Murder)，而非过失杀人 (Manslaughter)。

questions.question:
A defendant was charged with battery in a jurisdiction that follows the "retreat" doctrine, and he pleaded self-defense. At his trial, the evidence established the following: A man and his wife were enjoying a drink at a tavern when the defendant entered and stood near the door. The wife whispered to her husband that the defendant was the man who had insulted her on the street the day before. The husband approached the defendant and said, "Get out of here, or I'll break your nose." The defendant said, "Don't come any closer, or I'll hurt you." When the husband raised his fists menacingly, the defendant pulled a can of pepper spray from his pocket, aimed it at the husband's face, and sprayed. The husband fell to the floor, writhing in pain.
Should the defendant be convicted?

choices.a: No, because he had no obligation to retreat before resorting to nondeadly force in self-defense.
choices.b: No, because there is no obligation to retreat when one is in an occupied structure.
choices.c: Yes, because he failed to retreat even though there was an opportunity available.
choices.d: Yes, because the husband did not threaten to use deadly force against him.

data.questionStem:
Q85138

A defendant was charged with battery in a jurisdiction that follows the "retreat" doctrine, and he pleaded self-defense. At his trial, the evidence established the following: A man and his wife were enjoying a drink at a tavern when the defendant entered and stood near the door. The wife whispered to her husband that the defendant was the man who had insulted her on the street the day before. The husband approached the defendant and said, "Get out of here, or I'll break your nose." The defendant said, "Don't come any closer, or I'll hurt you." When the husband raised his fists menacingly, the defendant pulled a can of pepper spray from his pocket, aimed it at the husband's face, and sprayed. The husband fell to the floor, writhing in pain.

Should the defendant be convicted?

一名被告在一个遵循“退让”原则的司法管辖区被控伤害罪（battery），他以正当防卫为由进行抗辩。在其审判中，证据证实了以下事实：一名男子和他的妻子正在一家酒馆喝酒，此时被告进入并站在门边。妻子对丈夫耳语说，被告就是前一天在街上侮辱她的那个男人。丈夫走近被告说：“滚出去，否则我打烂你的鼻子。”被告说：“别再靠近了，否则我会伤害你。”当丈夫威胁性地举起拳头时，被告从口袋里掏出一罐胡椒喷雾，对准丈夫的脸部进行喷射。丈夫倒在地上，痛苦地扭动。

被告是否应被定罪？
options:
A. No, because he had no obligation to retreat before resorting to nondeadly force in self-defense.
不应定罪，因为他在为正当防卫而采取非致命武力之前，没有退让的义务。

B. No, because there is no obligation to retreat when one is in an occupied structure.
不应定罪，因为当一个人身处有人占用的建筑物内时，没有退让的义务。

C. Yes, because he failed to retreat even though there was an opportunity available.
应定罪，因为尽管有机会退让，他却没有退让。

D. Yes, because the husband did not threaten to use deadly force against him.
应定罪，因为丈夫并未威胁对他使用致命武力。
data.explanation:
Self-defense (justification for criminal conduct)


Duty to retreatGeneral requirements
Nondeadly forceNo duty to retreat
  • Actual & reasonable belief of imminent unlawful harm
  • Force reasonably necessary to prevent harm
  • Not initial aggressor
Deadly forceMajority rule: No duty to retreat
Minority rule: Duty when safe retreat available unless inside one's home
  • Actual & reasonable belief of imminent seriousharm or death
  • Deadly force necessary to prevent harm
  • Not initial aggressor
Battery occurs when a person inflicts harmful or offensive contact on another. But a battery committed in self-defense is justified - and not subject to criminal liability - if the person:

  • actually and reasonably believed that force was necessary to protect against imminent unlawful harm
  • used reasonable force (ie, no more than necessary) to prevent such harm and
  • was not the initial aggressor - ie, did not provoke the altercation.


There is no duty to retreat before using nondeadly force in self-defense - even when one could do so safely (Choice C). But in the few jurisdictions that follow the retreat doctrine (as seen here), a person must retreat before using deadly force when that person is outside his/her home and can retreat with reasonable safety.

Here, the wife provoked the altercation when she told her husband that the defendant had insulted her the day before. The husband then approached the defendant, threatened to break his nose, and raised his fists menacingly. This caused the defendant to actually and reasonably believe that he was in danger of imminent unlawful harm, so he sprayed the husband's face with pepper spray. And since the defendant had no duty to retreat before using such nondeadly force in self-defense, he should not be convicted of battery.

(Choice B) There is no obligation to retreat before using nondeadly force in self-defense - no matter the location. And under the castle doctrine (minority rule), there is no obligation to retreat before using deadly force while in one's home - not any occupied structure (eg, the tavern).

(Choice D) The fact that the husband did not threaten to use deadly force means that the defendant could not have used deadly force in self- defense. But since he used nondeadly force (pepper spray), his actions were justified.

Educational objective: Under the retreat doctrine (minority rule), a person must retreat before using deadly force in self-defense if that person is outside his/her home and can do so with reasonable safety. But there is no duty to retreat before using nondeadly force in self-defense.

选项正确率统计：A选项 53%（正确选项），B选项 1%，C选项 39%，D选项 5%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

正当防卫 (刑事行为的正当理由)


退让义务一般要求
非致命武力无退让义务
  • 对即将发生之非法伤害有真实且合理的相信
  • 为防止伤害而合理必要的武力
  • 非初始攻击者
致命武力多数规则：无退让义务
少数规则：当存在安全退让机会时有退让义务，除非身处自己家中
  • 对即将发生之严重伤害或死亡有真实且合理的相信
  • 为防止伤害而必要的致命武力
  • 非初始攻击者
当一个人对他人施加有害或冒犯性接触时，即构成伤害罪（Battery）。但是，为正当防卫而实施的伤害罪是正当的——且不负刑事责任——如果该人：

  • 真实且合理地相信，为防范即将发生的非法伤害，使用武力是必要的
  • 使用了合理的武力（即，不超过必要的程度）来防止此类伤害，并且
  • 不是初始攻击者——即，没有挑起争端。


在使用非致命武力进行正当防卫前，没有退让的义务——即使可以安全退让也无此义务（选项C）。但在少数遵循退让原则（retreat doctrine）的司法管辖区（如本案所示），当一个人身处家外且可以合理安全地退让时，在使用致命武力前必须退让。

在本案中，妻子告知丈夫被告前一天侮辱了她，从而挑起了争端。丈夫随后走近被告，威胁要打烂他的鼻子，并威胁性地举起拳头。这使得被告真实且合理地相信自己面临即将发生的非法伤害的危险，因此他用胡椒喷雾喷射了丈夫的脸部。并且，由于被告在使用此类非致命武力进行正当防卫前没有退让义务，他不应被判伤害罪。

（选项B） 在使用非致命武力进行正当防卫前，没有退让的义务——无论身在何处。并且，根据城堡原则（castle doctrine）（少数规则），当身处自己家中时，在使用致命武力前没有退让的义务——而非任何有人占用的建筑物（例如，本案中的酒馆）。

（选项D） 丈夫没有威胁使用致命武力这一事实，意味着被告不能使用致命武力进行正当防卫。但由于他使用了非致命武力（胡椒喷雾），他的行为是正当的。

教学目标：根据退让原则（retreat doctrine）（少数规则），当一个人身处家外且可以合理安全地退让时，在使用致命武力进行正当防卫前必须退让。但在使用非致命武力进行正当防卫前，没有退让的义务。

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law: Self-Defense
核心法则 (The Golden Rule) 在使用非致命武力 (Non-deadly Force) 进行正当防卫时，无论在何种司法管辖区，被告都没有退让的义务 (No duty to retreat)。

⚖️ 法律逻辑推演

1 界定武力等级
被告使用的是胡椒喷雾 (Pepper spray)。在法律上，这被视为非致命武力 (Non-deadly force)，因为它旨在致残或造成痛苦，而非造成死亡或严重身体伤害。
2 识别管辖区规则
题目明确指出该管辖区遵循“退让”原则 (Retreat Doctrine)。这是一个典型的 MBE 干扰项。
3 适用法律规则
“退让原则”仅适用于使用致命武力 (Deadly Force) 的情况。对于非致命武力，通用规则是：只要被告不是初始攻击者 (Initial Aggressor) 且合理相信面临非法武力威胁，即可反击，无需退让。

🔍 退让义务对比表

武力类型 退让原则管辖区
(Retreat Jurisdiction)
非致命武力
(Non-deadly)		 ❌ 无退让义务
(本题考点)
致命武力
(Deadly)		 ✅ 有退让义务
(如果能安全退让，且不在家中)
⚠️ 考场陷阱 (Exam Trap)
题目特意强调了这是一个 "Retreat Jurisdiction"，目的是诱导你选择 选项 C。

切记：看到“退让原则”时，第一反应必须是检查被告使用的是致命还是非致命武力。如果是非致命武力，退让原则不适用。

❌ 为什么其他选项是错误的？

  • 选项 B (错误)： 虽然提到了“有人占用的建筑物”，但这混淆了城堡原则 (Castle Doctrine)。城堡原则通常指在家中 (Home) 无需退让，而非任何建筑物。且本题关键在于非致命武力本身就无需退让，地点不是决定性因素。
  • 选项 D (错误)： 正当防卫并不要求对方必须使用致命武力。只要对方威胁使用非法武力（如本案中的拳头攻击），被告就可以使用适当的非致命武力进行反击。

A man who suffered from post-traumatic stress disorder became convinced that his neighbor was an evil demon. Truly believing that he needed to save the world from an evil demon, the man killed the neighbor. The man was charged with murder, and his defense attorney raised an insanity defense. During the trial, a psychiatrist testified that the man would not have killed the neighbor in the absence of his post-traumatic stress disorder and that the man did not think it was immoral to kill the neighbor because he believed the neighbor was an evil demon. The jurisdiction in which the court resides has adopted the M'Naghten test for insanity.
What is the man's strongest argument in support of an insanity defense?

choices.a: The man did not know the quality of the act he was performing.
choices.b: The man's acts were the product of a mental disease.
choices.c: The man did not know that his act was morally wrong.
choices.d: The man did not know the nature of the act he was performing.

questions.question:
A state statute provides: "The sale of an alcoholic beverage to any person under the age of 21 is a misdemeanor." A woman who was 20 years old, but who looked older and who had a very convincing fake driver's license indicating that she was 24, entered a convenience store, picked up a six-pack of beer, and placed the beer on the counter. The store clerk, after examining the driver's license, rang up the purchase. Both the clerk and the store owner were charged with violating the state statute. At trial, the court found both the clerk and store owner guilty.
What standard of liability must the court have interpreted the statute to impose?

choices.a: Strict liability only.
choices.b: Vicarious liability only.
choices.c: Both strict and vicarious liability.
choices.d: Either strict or vicarious liability.

data.questionStem:
Q85115

A state statute provides: "The sale of an alcoholic beverage to any person under the age of 21 is a misdemeanor." A woman who was 20 years old, but who looked older and who had a very convincing fake driver's license indicating that she was 24, entered a convenience store, picked up a six-pack of beer, and placed the beer on the counter. The store clerk, after examining the driver's license, rang up the purchase. Both the clerk and the store owner were charged with violating the state statute. At trial, the court found both the clerk and store owner guilty.

What standard of liability must the court have interpreted the statute to impose?

某州法规规定：“向任何未满21岁的人出售酒精饮料属于轻罪。”一名20岁的女子，但看起来比实际年龄大，并持有一张非常逼真的伪造驾照，显示她24岁。她进入一家便利店，拿起一提六瓶装的啤酒，并将其放在柜台上。店员在检查了驾照后，为她结了账。店员和店主均被指控违反该州法规。在审判中，法院裁定店员和店主均有罪。

法院必须将该法规解释为施加了何种责任标准？
options:
A. Strict liability only.
仅严格责任。

B. Vicarious liability only.
仅替代责任。

C. Both strict and vicarious liability.
严格责任和替代责任兼有。

D. Either strict or vicarious liability.
严格责任或替代责任之一。
data.explanation:
Most crimes require proof that a person committed a particular act (actus reus) with a particular state of mind (mens rea). But strict liability crimes have no mens rea requirement. This means that proof of the actus reus alone is sufficient to support a conviction. And persons can be directly liable for the strict liability crime if they commit the actus reus themselves OR vicariously liable if their agent (often an employee) does so.

Here, the clerk and store owner were convicted of violating the state statute after the clerk sold beer to a woman who was under 21 years of age (actus reus). But the clerk did not do so knowingly, or even negligently, since the woman looked older and the clerk examined her driver's license (no mens rea). Therefore, the court must have interpreted the statute as imposing strict liability to convict the clerk.

And since the store owner did not personally complete the sale, the court must have construed the statute as authorizing vicarious liability to convict the store owner for the sale by the clerk (the owner's agent) (Choices A, B, & D).

Educational objective: Strict liability crimes require a particular actus reus - but not a particular mens rea. And persons can be (1) directly liable for such crimes if they commit the actus reus themselves or (2) vicariously liable if their agent does so.



选项正确率统计：A选项 18%，B选项 2%，C选项 77%（正确选项），D选项 1%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

大多数犯罪要求证明行为人犯下了特定的行为（actus reus）并具有特定的精神状态（mens rea）。但是，严格责任犯罪没有 mens rea 的要求。这意味着仅凭 actus reus 的证据就足以支持定罪。并且，行为人若亲自实施 actus reus，则需为该严格责任犯罪承担直接责任；若其代理人（通常是雇员）实施该行为，则需承担替代责任。

在本案中，店员向一名未满21岁的女子出售啤酒（此为 actus reus），之后店员和店主均因违反州法规而被定罪。但店员的行为并非明知，甚至并非过失，因为该女子看起来年龄较大，且店员检查了她的驾照（无 mens rea）。因此，法院必须将该法规解释为施加严格责任，才能给店员定罪。

并且，由于店主并未亲自完成销售，法院必须将该法规解释为授权替代责任，才能因店员（店主的代理人）的销售行为而给店主定罪（因此选项A、B和D不正确）。

教学目标：严格责任犯罪要求有特定的 actus reus——但不需要特定的 mens rea。行为人可以 (1) 在亲自实施 actus reus 时为该等犯罪承担直接责任，或 (2) 在其代理人实施该行为时承担替代责任。

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考题解析

Criminal Law: General Principles
正确答案：C

本题考查的是刑法中的两个特殊责任原则：严格责任 (Strict Liability) 和 替代责任 (Vicarious Liability)。

核心法律概念
1. 严格责任 (Strict Liability)
不需要证明被告有 Mens Rea（犯罪意图/精神状态）。只要实施了 Actus Reus（犯罪行为），无论被告是否小心谨慎或出于善意，均构成犯罪。
2. 替代责任 (Vicarious Liability)
基于特定的关系（如雇主与雇员），一人需为另一人的犯罪行为承担责任，即使前者并未亲自参与该行为。
案情逻辑推演

为了理解为什么法院必须同时应用这两个原则，我们需要分别分析针对店员和店主的定罪逻辑：

1
针对店员 (The Clerk)：
店员检查了身份证，且该伪造证件“非常逼真”。这意味着店员既没有“故意”，也没有“鲁莽”，甚至没有“过失”。
如果该法规要求任何形式的 Mens Rea，店员都应被判无罪。
既然法院判决店员有罪，说明法院将该法规解释为严格责任犯罪（即：只要卖给了未成年人，无论怎么检查证件都构成犯罪）。
2
针对店主 (The Owner)：
店主根本不在场，也没有亲自实施销售行为（无 Actus Reus）。
在刑法中，通常不为他人的行为负责。
既然法院判决店主有罪，说明法院将该法规解释为允许替代责任，即雇主必须为雇员在工作范围内的违法行为负责。
结论

要同时支持这两个定罪结果，该法规必须被解释为：
1. 对行为人施加严格责任（定罪店员）；
2. 对雇主施加替代责任（定罪店主）。

因此，选项 C (Both strict and vicarious liability) 是唯一正确的逻辑推论。

💡 MBE 考试技巧 在 MBE 刑法题中，涉及公共福利犯罪 (Public Welfare Offenses)（如出售酒精、食品安全、药品监管、交通违规）时，常出现“严格责任”。

判断标准：如果题目强调被告“尽了最大努力”或“诚实地犯了错”（如本题中检查了逼真的假证），但依然被定罪，这通常是严格责任的标志。

questions.question:
Plagued by neighborhood youths who had been stealing lawn furniture from his backyard, a man remained awake nightly watching for them. One evening the man heard noises in his backyard. He yelled out, warning intruders to leave. Receiving no answer, he fired a shotgun filled with nonlethal buckshot into bushes along his back fence, where he believed the intruders might be hiding. A six-year-old boy was hiding in the bushes and was struck in the eye by some of the pellets, causing loss of sight. The man is charged with second-degree assault, which is defined in the jurisdiction as "maliciously causing serious physical injury to another."
What verdict should the jury render at the man's trial?

choices.a: Guilty, because the man recklessly caused serious physical injury.
choices.b: Guilty, because there is no privilege to use force against a person who is too young to be criminally responsible.
choices.c: Not guilty, because the child was trespassing and the man was using what he believed was nondeadly force.
choices.d: Not guilty, because the man did not intend to kill or to cause serious physical injury.

Q85086

Plagued by neighborhood youths who had been stealing lawn furniture from his backyard, a man remained awake nightly watching for them. One evening the man heard noises in his backyard. He yelled out, warning intruders to leave. Receiving no answer, he fired a shotgun filled with nonlethal buckshot into bushes along his back fence, where he believed the intruders might be hiding. A six-year-old boy was hiding in the bushes and was struck in the eye by some of the pellets, causing loss of sight. The man is charged with second-degree assault, which is defined in the jurisdiction as "maliciously causing serious physical injury to another."

What verdict should the jury render at the man's trial?

一名男子因其后院的草坪家具屡遭附近青少年偷窃而深受其扰，遂夜夜保持清醒，守候窃贼。一天晚上，该男子听到后院有响动。他大声喊叫，警告入侵者离开。在没有得到任何回应后，他向后院围栏边的灌木丛开了一枪，他认为入侵者可能藏在那里。枪中装的是非致命性的鹿弹。一名六岁的男孩正藏在灌木丛中，被一些弹丸击中眼睛，导致失明。该男子被控二级攻击罪 (second-degree assault)，该司法管辖区将其定义为“恶意对他人造成严重身体伤害”。

在该男子的审判中，陪审团应作出何种裁决？
options:
A. Guilty, because the man recklessly caused serious physical injury.
有罪，因为该男子鲁莽地造成了严重的身体伤害。

B. Guilty, because there is no privilege to use force against a person who is too young to be criminally responsible.
有罪，因为对一个因年龄太小而无刑事责任能力的人使用武力，并不享有特权。

C. Not guilty, because the child was trespassing and the man was using what he believed was nondeadly force.
无罪，因为该儿童正在非法侵入，而该男子使用的是他认为是'非致命性'的武力。

D. Not guilty, because the man did not intend to kill or to cause serious physical injury.
无罪，因为该男子无意杀人或造成严重身体伤害。

Justifications for criminal acts


NecessityReasonable belief that conduct was necessary to avoid imminent & substantial harm
No reasonable legal alternative
Harm caused < harm avoided
Self-defenseActual & reasonable belief that harm is imminent
Reasonable force used to prevent harm
Not initial aggressor
Defense of othersActual & reasonable belief that force is necessary to protect victim from imminent harm
Reasonable force used to protect victim
Defense of propertyForce reasonably necessary to prevent imminent & unlawful interference with possessed property
Nondeadly force used
Law enforcementPrevent imminent crime
Make lawful arrest or
Prevent suspect's escape from custody
Resisting arrestReasonable force permitted to resist unlawful arrest or arrest by unknown police officer
This jurisdiction defines second-degree assault as maliciously causing serious physical injury to another. Malice requires proof of either:
  • intent - conscious desire or practical certainty that one's act will cause a particular result or
  • recklessness - conscious disregard of a substantial and unjustifiable risk of harm.


Here, the man did not intend to kill or cause serious injury when he fired a shotgun filled with nonlethal buckshot into the bushes where he believed intruders might be hiding (Choice D). But he recklessly (ie, maliciously) disregarded the substantial and unjustifiable risk that this would cause serious physical injury. And since some of the pellets struck the boy in the eye, causing loss of sight, the man committed second-degree assault.

However, an assault committed in defense of property may be justified if the person (1) reasonably believed that property in his/her possession was in danger of imminent unlawful interference (eg, trespass) and (2) used reasonable, nondeadly force to prevent such interference. Here,

although the boy was trespassing and the man believed he was using nondeadly force, it was unreasonable to fire a shotgun into the bushes (Choice C). As a result, the man's use of force was not justified and he should be found guilty of second-degree assault.

(Choice B) The privilege to use force against another, whether in defense of one's self or property, does not turn on that person's age. But the person's age and characteristics may be considered in determining whether the use of force was reasonable.

Educational objective: An assault committed in defense of property may be justified if the person (1) reasonably believed that property in his/her possession was in danger of imminent unlawful interference and (2) used reasonable, nondeadly force to prevent such interference.

选项正确率统计：A选项 72%（正确选项），B选项 2%，C选项 16%，D选项 9%

刑事行为的正当化理由


紧急避险 (Necessity)有合理理由相信该行为对于避免即将来临的重大损害是必要的
无其他合理的法律替代方案
造成的损害 < 避免的损害
正当防卫 (Self-defense)事实上和有合理理由相信损害即将来临
为阻止损害而使用了合理的武力
非初始攻击者
为他人防卫 (Defense of others)事实上和有合理理由相信为保护受害者免受即将来临的损害而使用武力是必要的
为保护受害者而使用了合理的武力
财产防卫 (Defense of property)为防止对所占有财产的即将来临的非法干涉所合理必需的武力
使用非致命性武力
执法 (Law enforcement)阻止即将来临的犯罪
进行合法逮捕 或
防止嫌疑人从羁押中逃脱
抗拒逮捕 (Resisting arrest)允许使用合理武力以抗拒非法逮捕或身份不明的警察所进行的逮捕
该司法管辖区将二级攻击罪 (second-degree assault) 定义为恶意对他人造成严重身体伤害。恶意 (Malice) 要求证明以下任一情况：
  • 意图 (intent) - 有意识的愿望或实际上的确定性，即其行为将导致特定结果 或
  • 鲁莽 (recklessness) - 有意识地漠视重大且无理的损害风险。


在本案中，该男子向他认为入侵者可能藏身的灌木丛中开枪时，枪中装的是非致命性鹿弹，他并无意图杀人或造成严重伤害 (选项 D)。但他鲁莽地（即恶意地）漠视了此举可能导致严重身体伤害的重大且无理的风险。并且，由于部分弹丸击中了男孩的眼睛，导致其失明，因此该男子构成了二级攻击罪。

然而，在财产防卫 (defense of property)中实施的攻击行为在以下情况下可被视为正当：(1) 当事人有合理理由相信其占有的财产正面临即将来临的非法干涉（例如非法侵入）的危险，且 (2) 使用了合理的、非致命性的武力来阻止此类干涉。在本案中，

尽管男孩正在非法侵入，且该男子认为自己使用的是非致命性武力，但向灌木丛中开枪的行为是不合理的 (选项 C)。因此，该男子使用武力的行为不正当，应被裁定犯有二级攻击罪。

(选项 B) 对他人使用武力的特权，无论是为了自我防卫还是财产防卫，并不取决于对方的年龄。但是在判断使用武力是否合理时，可以考虑对方的年龄和特征。

教学目标：在财产防卫中实施的攻击行为在以下情况下可被视为正当：(1) 当事人有合理理由相信其占有的财产正面临即将来临的非法干涉的危险，且 (2) 使用了合理的、非致命性的武力来阻止此类干涉。

MBE 刑法考点解析

正确答案：A 有罪，因为该男子鲁莽地造成了严重的身体伤害。
(Guilty, because the man recklessly caused serious physical injury.)

核心考点：恶意的定义 (Definition of Malice)

本题的关键在于理解刑法中“恶意” (Malice) 的法律含义。在普通法 (Common Law) 和大多数司法管辖区中，恶意不仅仅指“故意” (Intent)，它包含两种心理状态：

  • 故意 (Intent): 明确希望造成特定结果。
  • 鲁莽 (Recklessness): 有意识地漠视一个重大且无理的风险 (Substantial and Unjustifiable Risk)。

详细推理逻辑

要判定该男子犯有二级攻击罪 (Second-degree Assault)，必须满足两个要素：

  1. 行为 (Actus Reus): 造成他人严重身体伤害。
    -> 事实：男孩眼睛失明，属于严重伤害。
  2. 意图 (Mens Rea): 恶意 (Maliciously)。
    -> 分析：虽然男子可能没有“致人失明”的直接意图（排除选项 D），但他向认为有人藏身的灌木丛开枪，这显然制造了极高的受伤风险。

即使使用的是“非致命性”鹿弹 (Nonlethal buckshot)，向不明身份的人员方向盲射，构成了对重大风险的有意识漠视 (Conscious Disregard)。这种心理状态在法律上即为鲁莽 (Recklessness)，足以满足“恶意”的要求。

为什么“财产防卫”不能免责？

考生常误选 选项 C，认为这是合法的财产防卫 (Defense of Property)。

法律规则：

  • 你可以使用非致命性武力 (Non-deadly force) 保护财产。
  • 关键限制：使用的武力必须是合理的 (Reasonable)。

本案分析：虽然男孩是侵入者 (Trespasser)，但仅仅为了保护草坪家具，就向黑暗中的灌木丛开枪（即使是非致命弹药），这种行为被法律视为不合理的武力使用。因此，防卫特权丧失。

其他选项错在哪里？

  • 选项 B 错误： 这是一个干扰项。使用武力的特权并不取决于受害者的年龄。如果武力是合理的，即使对方是儿童也可能免责；反之，如果武力不合理，对方是成年人也有罪。
  • 选项 C 错误： 见上文分析。虽然是侵入者，但被告使用的武力在当时情况下是不合理的 (Unreasonable)。
  • 选项 D 错误： 这是对“恶意”定义的误解。恶意不需要特定的杀人或伤害意图，鲁莽 (Recklessness) 足以构成恶意。
🎓 MBE 考试技巧

当题目中出现"Maliciously" (恶意地) 这个词时，千万不要只联想到“邪恶的意图”或“故意”。在刑法题中，第一反应应当是检查是否符合 Recklessness (鲁莽) 的标准。

此外，凡是涉及Defense of Property (财产防卫)，如果使用了枪支（即使未造成死亡），通常会被认定为武力过当或不合理，除非有人身安全的威胁。

questions.question:
A kidnapping statute in State A makes it a crime for a person, including a parent, to "take a child from the custody of his custodial parent, knowing he has no privilege to do so." After a bitter court battle, a woman and man were divorced, and the woman was given custody of their daughter.
The man later moved to State B, where he brought an action to obtain custody of the daughter. A local judge awarded him custody. His attorney incorrectly advised him that, under this award, he was entitled to take the daughter away from the woman. The man drove to State A, picked the daughter up at her preschool, and took her back to State B with him. He was indicted for kidnapping in State A, extradited from State B, and tried.
At trial, he testified that he had relied on his attorney's advice in taking the daughter, and that at the time he believed his conduct was not illegal.
If the jury believes the man's testimony, what should be its finding?

choices.a: Acquitted, because he acted on the advice of an attorney.
choices.b: Acquitted, because he lacked a necessary mental element of the crime.
choices.c: Convicted, because reliance on an attorney's advice is not a defense.
choices.d: Convicted, provided a reasonable person would have known that the attorney's advice was erroneous.

data.questionStem:
Q85141

A kidnapping statute in State A makes it a crime for a person, including a parent, to "take a child from the custody of his custodial parent, knowing he has no privilege to do so." After a bitter court battle, a woman and man were divorced, and the woman was given custody of their daughter.

The man later moved to State B, where he brought an action to obtain custody of the daughter. A local judge awarded him custody. His attorney incorrectly advised him that, under this award, he was entitled to take the daughter away from the woman. The man drove to State A, picked the daughter up at her preschool, and took her back to State B with him. He was indicted for kidnapping in State A, extradited from State B, and tried.

At trial, he testified that he had relied on his attorney's advice in taking the daughter, and that at the time he believed his conduct was not illegal.

If the jury believes the man's testimony, what should be its finding?

A州的绑架法规规定，任何人，包括父母，“在明知无权的情况下，将子女从其监护父母的监护下带走”，即构成犯罪。

在一场激烈的法庭斗争后，一名女子和一名男子离婚，女子获得了他们女儿的监护权。

该男子后来搬到B州，并在那里提起诉讼以获得女儿的监护权。当地一名法官将监护权判给了他。他的律师错误地告知他，根据这项判决，他有权将女儿从女子身边带走。该男子开车前往A州，从女儿的幼儿园接走她，并把她带回了B州。他在A州因绑架罪被起诉，从B州被引渡，并接受审判。

在审判中，他作证称，他在带走女儿时是依据其律师的建议行事，并且当时他相信自己的行为并非违法。

如果陪审团相信该男子的证词，应作出何种裁定？
options:
A. Acquitted, because he acted on the advice of an attorney.
无罪，因为他根据律师的建议行事。

B. Acquitted, because he lacked a necessary mental element of the crime.
无罪，因为他缺乏该罪行必要的犯罪意图要素。

C. Convicted, because reliance on an attorney's advice is not a defense.
有罪，因为信赖律师的建议不构成抗辩理由。

D. Convicted, provided a reasonable person would have known that the attorney's advice was erroneous.
有罪，前提是一个理性人本应知道该律师的建议是错误的。
data.explanation:
Mistake of law v. Mistake of fact


DefinitionApplicability
Mistake of lawDefendant mistakenly believes conduct not prohibited by lawNo defense unless:
  • Law prohibiting conduct was unavailable
  • Defendant reasonably relied on invalid law
  • Mistake negates mens rea
Mistake of factDefendant is mistaken as to a matter of factWhen mistake negates mens rea:
  • Specific intent - defense if honest mistake
  • General intent & malice - defense if honest & reasonable mistake
  • Strict liability - no defense
Mens rea - state of mind necessary to be guilty of criminal offense

A defendant's mistaken belief that his/her conduct was not prohibited by law (ie, mistake of law ) is rarely a defense to criminal liability. But it is a valid defense when it negates the required mens rea (ie, mental state) for the crime.

Here, State A's kidnapping statute makes it a crime for any person to take a child from his/her custodial parent, knowing that he/she has no privilege to do so. And though the man took the daughter away from the woman (her custodial parent) in State A, his attorney had incorrectly advised him that he was legally entitled to take her. As a result, the man's mistake of law negates the necessary mental element of the crime, and he should be acquitted.

(Choices A, C & D) Erroneous legal advice from an attorney is not itself a valid defense - regardless of whether a reasonable person would have known that the advice was erroneous or relied on it. But it may negate the required mental state for the crime (as seen here). In that case, a mistake-of-law defense is appropriate.

Educational objective: A defendant's mistaken belief that his/her conduct was not prohibited by law (ie, mistake of law) is a defense to a crime when it negates the required mens rea.

选项正确率统计：A选项 3%，B选项 78%（正确选项），C选项 16%，D选项 1%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

法律错误与事实错误之比较


定义适用性
法律错误被告错误地认为其行为未被法律禁止不构成抗辩理由，除非：
  • 禁止该行为的法律尚未公布
  • 被告合理地信赖了一项无效的法律
  • 该错误排除了犯罪意图(mens rea)
事实错误被告对某一事实存在错误认知当该错误排除犯罪意图(mens rea)时：
  • 特定意图犯罪 - 如果是善意错误，则构成抗辩理由
  • 一般意图犯罪与恶意犯罪 - 如果是善意且合理的错误，则构成抗辩理由
  • 严格责任犯罪 - 不构成抗辩理由
Mens rea - 构成刑事犯罪所必需的心理状态

被告错误地认为其行为未被法律禁止（即法律错误），这很少能成为刑事责任的抗辩理由。但当它排除了该罪行所要求的犯罪意图(mens rea)（即心理状态）时，它就是一个有效的抗辩理由。

在本案中，A州的绑架法规规定，任何人在明知无权的情况下将子女从其监护父母处带走，即构成犯罪。尽管该男子在A州将女儿从女子（其监护父母）身边带走，但他的律师错误地告知他，他有合法权利带走她。因此，该男子的法律错误排除了该罪行必要的犯罪意图要素，他应被宣告无罪。

（选项A、C和D）律师的错误法律建议本身并不是一个有效的抗辩理由——无论一个理性人是否本应知道该建议是错误的，或是否信赖了该建议。但它可能排除该罪行所要求的心理状态（如本案所示）。在这种情况下，以法律错误作为抗辩理由是恰当的。

教学目标：当被告错误地认为其行为未被法律禁止（即法律错误）并且该错误排除了所要求的犯罪意图(mens rea)时，这可以成为一项针对犯罪的抗辩理由。

MBE Criminal Law

法律错误与犯罪意图

正确答案：B 无罪，因为他缺乏该罪行必要的犯罪意图要素。
(Acquitted, because he lacked a necessary mental element of the crime.)
核心法律原则解析

本题考察的核心是法律错误 (Mistake of Law) 何时可以作为刑事抗辩理由。

一般原则 (General Rule)：
通常情况下，“不知法不免责” (Ignorantia juris non excusat)。仅仅因为被告不知道自己的行为违法，或者错误地认为自己的行为合法，并不能作为抗辩理由。
关键例外 (The Exception)：
如果法律错误导致被告缺乏该犯罪所必需的特定心理状态 (Negates the Mens Rea)，则该错误可以作为抗辩理由。
本案逻辑推演

要判定被告是否有罪，必须严格分析题目中给出的法条定义：

  1. 法条要素：A州法律规定绑架罪的要素是“将子女从监护父母处带走，且明知 (Knowing) 自己无权 (Privilege) 这样做”。
  2. 犯罪意图 (Mens Rea)：这是一个特定意图 (Specific Intent) 类型的要求。检方必须证明被告在带走孩子时，主观上“知道”自己是没有权利的。
  3. 事实应用：
    • 被告咨询了律师。
    • 律师（错误地）告诉他，根据B州的判决，他有权带走孩子。
    • 被告相信了律师，认为自己有权带走孩子。
  4. 结论：由于被告真诚地相信自己有权带走孩子，他就不具备“明知自己无权”这一必要的心理要素。因此，犯罪构成要件不完整，应当无罪。
为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 A：无罪，因为他根据律师建议行事

错误原因：单纯“听从律师建议” (Reliance on counsel) 本身并不是一个独立的抗辩理由。它之所以在本案有效，仅仅是因为它帮助证明了被告缺乏犯罪意图。如果法条是严格责任 (Strict Liability)，即使听了律师建议也是有罪的。

选项 C & D：有罪...

错误原因：这两个选项忽略了法条中明确规定的“明知 (Knowing)”这一心理要素。无论律师的建议多么离谱，只要被告真的信了，他就没有“明知自己违法”。

MBE 解题技巧

在处理刑法题目时，第一步永远是仔细阅读题目中给出的法条定义。

如果法条中包含表示特定心理状态的词汇，如：

  • Knowing (明知)
  • With intent to (意图...)
  • Purposefully (故意地/有目的地)

那么任何导致被告未能形成该心理状态的错误（无论是事实错误还是法律错误），通常都是有效的抗辩理由。

questions.question:
A husband and wife took their 12-year-old son to a political rally in an auditorium to hear a controversial United States senator speak. The speaker was late, and the wife stepped outside the auditorium to smoke a cigarette. While there, she saw a man placing what she believed to be a bomb against the back wall of the auditorium. She went back inside and told her husband what she had seen. Without alerting anyone, they took their son and left. Some 20 minutes later, the bomb exploded, killing eight persons and injuring 50.
In the jurisdiction, murder in the first degree is defined as an intentional homicide committed with premeditation and deliberation; murder in the second degree is defined as all other murder at common law; and manslaughter is defined as either a homicide in the heat of passion arising from adequate provocation or a homicide caused by gross negligence or reckless indifference to consequence.
As to the deaths of the eight persons, what crime, if any, did the wife commit?

choices.a: Manslaughter.
choices.b: Murder in the first degree.
choices.c: Murder in the second degree.
choices.d: No crime.

The speaker was late, and the wife stepped outside the auditorium to smoke a cigarette. While there, she saw a man placing what she believed to be a bomb against the back wall of the auditorium. She went back inside and told her husband what she had seen. Without alerting anyone, they took their son and left. Some 20 minutes later, the bomb exploded, killing eight persons and injuring 50.

In the jurisdiction, murder in the first degree is defined as an intentional homicide committed with premeditation and deliberation; murder in the second degree is defined as all other murder at common law; and manslaughter is defined as either a homicide in the heat of passion arising from adequate provocation or a homicide caused by gross negligence or reckless indifference to consequence.

As to the deaths of the eight persons, what crime, if any, did the wife commit?

一对夫妻带着他们12岁的儿子去一个礼堂参加政治集会，聆听一位有争议的美国参议员的演讲。演讲者迟到了，妻子走出礼堂去抽烟。在外面时，她看到一名男子将她认为是炸弹的东西放在礼堂的后墙上。她回到礼堂内，将所见之事告诉了丈夫。他们没有警告任何人，就带着儿子离开了。大约20分钟后，炸弹爆炸，造成8人死亡，50人受伤。

在该司法管辖区，一级谋杀罪（murder in the first degree）的定义是经过预谋和深思熟虑后实施的故意杀人行为；二级谋杀罪（murder in the second degree）的定义是普通法（common law）上的所有其他谋杀行为；而过失杀人罪（manslaughter）的定义是因充分的挑衅而一时激愤下实施的杀人行为，或因重大过失或对后果鲁莽漠视而造成的杀人行为。

就这八人的死亡而言，该妻子犯了什么罪行（如有）？
options:
A. Manslaughter.
过失杀人罪。

B. Murder in the first degree.
一级谋杀罪。

C. Murder in the second degree.
二级谋杀罪。

D. No crime.
未构成犯罪。
data.explanation:
To commit criminal homicide, a person must unlawfully kill another (actus reus) with the requisite mental state (mens rea). Criminal liability typically stems from a voluntary act - an overt movement over which the defendant has conscious control (eg, deliberately pulling a gun's trigger). But criminal liability can also arise from a failure to act (ie, omission) if the defendant had a legal duty to act and could have reasonably done so.

A legal duty to act can arise under any of the following circumstances:
  • The defendant and the victim are in a special relationship (eg, parent/child, spouses).
  • The defendant assumed the victim's care by rendering aid.
  • The defendant's conduct created the risk of harm to the victim.
  • A statute imposes a duty.
  • A contract imposes a duty.

Here, the wife saw a man place what appeared to be a bomb in the auditorium. She told her husband, and they left with their son. The bomb went off shortly thereafter and killed eight people. Although the wife had a legal duty to protect her husband and son from the bomb based on their special relationship, she had no legal duty to warn anyone else. Therefore, she did not commit any degree of criminal homicide - first-degree murder, second-degree murder, or manslaughter (Choices A, B, & C).

Educational objective: A person is not criminally liable for failing to act unless he/she had a legal duty to do so. A legal duty can be based on (1) a special relationship, (2) assumption of care, (3) creation of the risk of harm, (4) a statute, or (5) a contract.



选项正确率统计：A选项 7%，B选项 0%，C选项 0%，D选项 91%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

要构成刑事杀人罪，行为人必须非法致死他人（犯罪行为），并具备必要的犯罪意图（犯罪心理）。刑事责任通常源于自愿行为——即被告有意识控制下的外在行动（例如，故意扣动扳机）。但是，如果被告有法律义务去行动并且能够合理地做到，那么刑事责任也可能因不作为（即疏忽）而产生。

采取行动的法律义务可能在以下任何一种情况下产生：
  • 被告与受害者之间存在特殊关系（例如，父母/子女，配偶）。
  • 被告通过提供援助而承担了照顾受害者的责任。
  • 被告的行为给受害者带来了伤害风险。
  • 法规规定了义务。
  • 合同规定了义务。

在本案中，妻子看到一名男子将看似炸弹的物体放置在礼堂内。她告诉了丈夫，然后他们带着儿子离开了。不久后炸弹爆炸，造成八人死亡。尽管基于他们的特殊关系，妻子有法律义务保护她的丈夫和儿子免受炸弹的伤害，但她没有法律义务警告任何其他人。因此，她没有犯任何程度的刑事杀人罪——无论是一级谋杀罪、二级谋杀罪还是过失杀人罪（选项 A、B 和 C）。

教学目标：除非一个人有法律义务去行动，否则他/她不因不作为而承担刑事责任。法律义务可以基于（1）特殊关系，（2）承担照顾责任，（3）制造伤害风险，（4）法规，或（5）合同。

MBE 刑法考点解析

Criminal Law: Omission & Duty
✅ 正确答案：选项 D 未构成犯罪 (No crime)。

妻子对礼堂内的陌生人没有法律上的行动义务，因此她的不作为不构成犯罪。

⚖️ 核心法律规则
要在美国刑法下承担刑事责任，通常需要一个自愿行为 (Voluntary Act)。

不作为 (Omission) 只有在被告对受害者负有法律义务 (Legal Duty) 时，才构成犯罪行为 (Actus Reus)。
🔍 法律义务的五大来源

如果不存在以下情况之一，即使见死不救，在普通法下通常也无罪：

1️⃣
法规规定 (Statute)
e.g., filing tax returns.
2️⃣
合同义务 (Contract)
e.g., lifeguard, nurse.
3️⃣
特殊关系 (Special Relationship)
e.g., parent-child, spouse-spouse.
4️⃣
自愿承担照顾 (Assumption of Care)
Starting to rescue and then stopping.
5️⃣
制造危险 (Creation of Peril)
Defendant caused the risk (even innocently).
📝 本案案情分析

1. 妻子的行为：
她看到了炸弹，告诉了丈夫，并带走了家人。她没有警告其他人。这属于不作为 (Omission)。

2. 是否存在法律义务？

  • 特殊关系？ 她与丈夫和儿子有特殊关系，但她已经救了他们。她与礼堂里的其他听众没有特殊关系。
  • 制造危险？ 炸弹是别人放的，不是她放的。
  • 合同/法规？ 题目未提及她是保安或有相关法规。

3. 结论：
尽管她在道德上可能受到谴责，但在法律上，她对陌生人没有“救助义务” (No Duty to Rescue)。没有法律义务，就没有犯罪行为 (Actus Reus)，因此不构成任何犯罪。

❌ 为什么其他选项错误

选项 A (过失杀人), B (一级谋杀), C (二级谋杀)：

所有这些罪行都需要证明被告实施了非法的“杀人行为”。由于妻子没有法律义务去警告他人，她的沉默不是法律意义上的“致死行为”。无论她的心态是否鲁莽 (Reckless) 或恶意 (Malice)，没有犯罪行为 (Actus Reus) 就没有犯罪。

💡 MBE 考试技巧
在处理“不作为”题目时，切勿用道德标准代替法律标准。

即使结果非常悲惨（如本案8人死亡），只要被告没有上述5种法律义务之一，答案通常就是“无罪”。一定要先寻找义务的来源 (Source of Duty)。

questions.question:
A man, despondent and angry over losing his job, was contemplating suicide. With his revolver in his pocket, he went to a bar and drank until he was very intoxicated. He overheard a customer on the next barstool telling the bartender how it was necessary for companies to downsize in order to keep the economy strong. The man turned to the customer and said, "Why don't you shut the hell up." The customer responded, "This is a free country, and I can say what I want," all the while shaking his finger at the man. The man became enraged, snatched his revolver from his pocket, and shot the customer, killing him.
A state statute defines first-degree murder as "knowingly causing the death of another person after deliberation upon the matter." Deliberation is defined as "cool reflection for any length of time, no matter how brief." Second-degree murder is defined as "knowingly causing the death of another person." Manslaughter is defined as at common law.
What crime did the man commit?

choices.a: First-degree murder, because deliberation can take place in an instant.
choices.b: First-degree murder, because he contemplated taking a human life before becoming intoxicated.
choices.c: Manslaughter, because there was a reasonable explanation for his becoming enraged.
choices.d: Second-degree murder, because he knowingly caused the customer's death without deliberation.

Q85092

A man, despondent and angry over losing his job, was contemplating suicide. With his revolver in his pocket, he went to a bar and drank until he was very intoxicated. He overheard a customer on the next barstool telling the bartender how it was necessary for companies to downsize in order to keep the economy strong. The man turned to the customer and said, "Why don't you shut the hell up." The customer responded, "This is a free country, and I can say what I want," all the while shaking his finger at the man. The man became enraged, snatched his revolver from his pocket, and shot the customer, killing him.

A state statute defines first-degree murder as "knowingly causing the death of another person after deliberation upon the matter." Deliberation is defined as "cool reflection for any length of time, no matter how brief." Second-degree murder is defined as "knowingly causing the death of another person." Manslaughter is defined as at common law.

What crime did the man commit?

一名男子因失业而心灰意冷、怒火中烧，当时正考虑自杀。他口袋里揣着左轮手枪，去了一家酒吧，一直喝酒直到酩酊大醉。他无意中听到邻座的一位顾客告诉酒保，为了保持经济强劲，公司裁员是必要的。该男子转向那位顾客说：“你他妈的怎么不闭嘴。”顾客回应道：“这是个自由的国家，我想说什么就说什么。”，同时还用手指着该男子。该男子勃然大怒，从口袋里掏出左轮手枪，开枪射杀了那名顾客。

某州法规将一级谋杀罪（first-degree murder）定义为“在对事件进行深思熟虑后，故意致使他人死亡”。深思熟虑（Deliberation）被定义为“任何时长的冷静思考，无论多么短暂”。二级谋杀罪（Second-degree murder）被定义为“故意致使他人死亡”。Manslaughter罪则按照普通法（common law）的定义。

该男子犯了什么罪？
options:
A. First-degree murder, because deliberation can take place in an instant.
一级谋杀罪（First-degree murder），因为深思熟虑（deliberation）可以瞬间发生。

B. First-degree murder, because he contemplated taking a human life before becoming intoxicated.
一级谋杀罪（First-degree murder），因为他在醉酒前曾考虑过夺取一个人的生命。

C. Manslaughter, because there was a reasonable explanation for his becoming enraged.
Manslaughter罪，因为他勃然大怒有合理的解释。

D. Second-degree murder, because he knowingly caused the customer's death without deliberation.
二级谋杀罪（Second-degree murder），因为他在没有深思熟虑（deliberation）的情况下故意导致了顾客的死亡。
data.explanation:
Intoxication


VoluntaryDeliberate ingestion of substance that person knew or should have known has intoxicating effects
InvoluntaryUnknowing or forcible ingestion of intoxicating substance
In this state, criminal homicide - the killing of another with the requisite mens rea (ie, state of mind) - is divided into three levels:
  • First-degree murder - knowingly killing another after deliberation (ie, cool reflection for any length of time, no matter how brief)
  • Second-degree murder - knowingly killing another (ie, acting with substantial certainty that death will occur)
  • Common law manslaughter - intentionally killing another in the heat of passion upon adequate provocation or in imperfect self-defense (voluntary manslaughter) or unintentionally killing another with criminal negligence or during an unlawful act (involuntary manslaughter)


Voluntary intoxication is the deliberate ingestion of a substance that a person knows or should know has intoxicating effects. This is a defense to specific intent crimes if the intoxication prevented the person from forming such intent. First-degree murder is a specific intent crime since it requires a person to deliberate upon the killing, so voluntary intoxication is a defense. But it is not a defense to second-degree murder since that crime requires a lesser mental state (ie, knowledge).

Here, the state statute establishes that deliberation can take place instantly. But the man's intoxication prevented him from deliberating upon the killing since he killed in a rage - not after cool reflection. Therefore, he did not commit first-degree murder (Choice A). However, the man knowingly killed the customer since it was substantially certain that the customer would die from being shot at close range. And since his intoxication did not negate that knowledge, the man still committed second-degree murder.

(Choice B) Voluntary intoxication is not a defense to first-degree murder when the defendant contemplated killing another person before becoming intoxicated. Here, the man contemplated killing himself (not another) before becoming intoxicated, so voluntary intoxication is an available defense.

(Choice C) Voluntary manslaughter is the intentional killing of another in response to adequate provocation - ie, conduct that would cause a reasonable person to lose control (more than mere words). Here, the man became enraged when the customer said, "This is a free country, and I can say what I want" while shaking his finger. Since that would not provoke a reasonable person to kill, the man did not commit voluntary manslaughter.

Educational objective: Voluntary intoxication - deliberately ingesting a substance that a person knows or should know has intoxicating effects - is a defense to specific intent crimes (eg, first-degree murder) when the intoxication prevented the person from forming such intent.

醉酒


自愿在明知或应知某种物质具有致醉效果的情况下，蓄意摄入该物质
非自愿在不知情或被强迫的情况下摄入致醉物质
在该州，刑事杀人罪——即以必要的犯罪意图（mens rea，即精神状态）杀害他人——分为三个级别：
  • 一级谋杀罪（First-degree murder）——在深思熟虑（deliberation，即无论多么短暂的冷静思考）后故意杀害他人
  • 二级谋杀罪（Second-degree murder） - 故意杀害他人（即在基本确信死亡会发生的情况下行事）
  • 普通法上的Manslaughter罪——因受到充分挑衅而在盛怒之下故意杀人，或在不完美的自卫中杀人（voluntary manslaughter，即故意manslaughter）或因刑事过失或在从事非法行为过程中非故意杀人（involuntary manslaughter，即非故意manslaughter）


自愿醉酒是指在明知或应知某种物质具有致醉效果的情况下蓄意摄入该物质。如果醉酒状态使行为人无法形成特定的犯罪意图，则这可作为特定意图犯罪（specific intent crimes）的一项抗辩理由。一级谋杀罪（First-degree murder）是一种特定意图犯罪，因为它要求行为人对杀人行为进行深思熟虑，因此自愿醉酒可作为一项抗辩理由。但它不能作为二级谋杀罪的抗辩理由，因为该罪行要求一个较低程度的精神状态（即“明知”）。

在本案中，该州法规规定，深思熟虑（deliberation）可以瞬间完成。但该男子的醉酒状态使他无法对杀人行为进行深思熟虑，因为他是在盛怒之下杀人——而非经过冷静思考。因此，他没有犯下一级谋杀罪（选项A）。然而，该男子是故意（knowingly）杀害了顾客，因为在近距离射击的情况下，顾客的死亡是基本确定的。由于他的醉酒状态并未否定这种“明知”，该男子仍然构成了二级谋杀罪。

（选项B）当被告人在醉酒前曾考虑杀害他人时，自愿醉酒不能作为一级谋杀罪的抗辩理由。在本案中，该男子在醉酒前考虑的是杀害自己（而非他人），因此自愿醉酒是可用的抗辩理由。

（选项C）Voluntary manslaughter（故意manslaughter）是指为回应充分挑衅而故意杀害他人——即，该挑衅行为足以导致一个理性的人失去控制（不仅仅是言语上的挑衅）。在本案中，当顾客一边摇着手指一边说“这是个自由的国家，我想说什么就说什么”时，该男子勃然大怒。由于这并不足以激怒一个理性的人去杀人，因此该男子没有犯下voluntary manslaughter罪。

教学目标：自愿醉酒——即在明知或应知某种物质具有致醉效果的情况下蓄意摄入——在醉酒状态妨碍行为人形成特定犯罪意图时，可作为特定意图犯罪（例如，一级谋杀罪）的抗辩理由。

MBE 刑法考点解析

Homicide & Intoxication Defense
✅ 正确答案：选项 D

二级谋杀罪 (Second-degree murder)，因为他在没有深思熟虑 (deliberation) 的情况下故意导致了顾客的死亡。

核心考点：自愿醉酒与犯罪意图

本题主要考察自愿醉酒 (Voluntary Intoxication) 是否可以作为杀人罪的抗辩理由。在 MBE 考试中，这是一个经典的“特定意图”与“一般意图”区分的考点。

规则 (The Rule)：

自愿醉酒可以否定特定意图 (Specific Intent)，但通常不能否定一般意图 (General Intent) 或恶意 (Malice)。

根据题目中的法规定义：

  • 一级谋杀 需要“深思熟虑” (Deliberation)。这属于特定意图。如果醉酒导致被告无法进行“冷静思考”，则不能定一级谋杀。
  • 二级谋杀 只需要“故意” (Knowingly)。在刑法分级中，这通常被视为恶意犯罪 (Malice Crime) 或一般意图的范畴，自愿醉酒通常不是有效的抗辩。
案情具体分析

1. 为什么不是一级谋杀？(排除 A 和 B)

虽然法规说深思熟虑可以瞬间发生，但事实表明该男子当时处于“酩酊大醉” (very intoxicated) 且“勃然大怒” (enraged) 的状态。这种状态在法律上阻止了他进行“冷静思考” (cool reflection)。

关于选项 B： 他在醉酒前考虑的是自杀，而不是杀害被害人。这种预谋不能转移到被害人身上来构成一级谋杀。

2. 为什么不是 Manslaughter？(排除 C)

普通法上的 Voluntary Manslaughter (激情杀人) 要求存在充分的挑衅 (Adequate Provocation)。

法律上的铁律是：“言语挑衅不足以构成充分挑衅” (Mere words are not adequate provocation)。无论受害者的话多么难听（“自由国家”、“我想说什么就说什么”），或者伴随手指指点的动作，这在法律上都不足以让一个理性的人失去理智去杀人。

3. 为什么是二级谋杀？(选中 D)

尽管男子醉酒，但他仍然能够形成“故意” (Knowingly) 的心理状态。他从口袋掏枪并近距离射击，法律推定他“明知”这会导致死亡。由于自愿醉酒不能作为二级谋杀（恶意/一般意图犯罪）的抗辩，因此他的行为符合二级谋杀的定义。

MBE 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)

看到“醉酒” (Intoxication) 的题目，立刻思考：

  1. 这是特定意图犯罪吗？(如：一级谋杀、盗窃、抢劫、入室盗窃)。如果是，醉酒可能是抗辩。
  2. 这是恶意犯罪或一般意图犯罪吗？(如：二级谋杀、纵火、殴打)。如果是，醉酒通常无效。

本题中，醉酒帮他免除了一级谋杀（特定意图），但他掉进了二级谋杀（恶意/明知）的网中。

questions.question:
A worker at a day-care center run by a corporation noticed that one of the boys often arrived with bruises and welts on his back and legs. A statute in the jurisdiction requires all day-care workers to report to the police cases where there is probable cause to suspect child abuse and provides for immediate removal from the home of any suspected child-abuse victims. The worker was not aware of this statute. Nevertheless, he did report the boy's condition to his supervisor, who advised him to keep quiet about it so the day-care center would not get into trouble for defaming a parent. About two weeks after the worker first noticed the boy's condition, the boy was beaten to death by his father.
The worker has been charged with murder in the death of the boy. The evidence at trial disclosed, in addition to the above, that the boy had been the victim of beatings by the father for some time, and that these earlier beatings had been responsible for the marks that the worker had seen. The boy's mother had been aware of the beatings but had not stopped them because she was herself afraid of the boy's father.
What is the worker's best argument that he is NOT guilty of murder?

choices.a: He lacked the mental state necessary to the commission of the crime.
choices.b: He was not aware of the duty-to-report statute.
choices.c: His omission was not the proximate cause of the boy's death.
choices.d: The day-care corporation, rather than the worker, was guilty of the omission, which was sanctioned by its supervisory-level agent.

The boy's mother had been aware of the beatings but had not stopped them because she was herself afraid of the boy's father.

What is the worker's best argument that he is NOT guilty of murder?

一家公司经营的日托中心的一名工作人员注意到，其中一个男孩经常带着背部和腿上的瘀伤和伤痕来到中心。该司法管辖区的一项法规要求所有日托中心工作人员在有合理理由（probable cause）怀疑存在虐待儿童的情况下向警方报告，并规定应立即将任何疑似受虐儿童从其家中带离。该工作人员并不知道这项法规。尽管如此，他还是将男孩的情况报告给了他的主管，主管建议他对这件事保持沉默，以免日托中心因诽谤家长而惹上麻烦。在该工作人员首次注意到男孩的情况大约两周后，男孩被其父亲殴打致死。

该工作人员因男孩的死亡被控犯有谋杀罪。庭审证据显示，除上述情况外，该男孩一段时间以来一直是其父亲殴打的受害者，并且这些早期的殴打造成了该工作人员所看到的伤痕。男孩的母亲知道这些殴打行为，但没有制止，因为她自己也害怕男孩的父亲。

该工作人员主张自己不构成谋杀罪的最佳论点是什么？
options:
A. He lacked the mental state necessary to the commission of the crime.
他缺乏实施该罪行所必需的犯罪意图（mental state）。

B. He was not aware of the duty-to-report statute.
他不知道有报告义务的法规。

C. His omission was not the proximate cause of the boy's death.
他的不作为并非男孩死亡的近因（proximate cause）。

D. The day-care corporation, rather than the worker, was guilty of the omission, which was sanctioned by its supervisory-level agent.
是日托公司，而非该工作人员，对该不作为负有罪责，该不作为已获得其主管级代理人的批准。
data.explanation:
Murder is the unlawful killing of another (criminal act) with malice aforethought (mental state). An unlawful killing can be caused by a voluntary act (eg, deliberately pulling a gun's trigger). But it can also be caused by an omission - ie, a failure to perform a statutory or other legal duty when the defendant could have reasonably done so. Causation must be both:
  • actual - (1) the victim would not have died at that time but for the defendant's conduct or (2) when there were multiple causes, the defendant's conduct was a substantial factor in the victim's death and
  • proximate - the death was a natural and probable (ie, foreseeable) consequence of the defendant's conduct.


Here, the worker failed to perform his statutory duty to report the boy's frequent bruises and welts to police even though he reasonably could have done so (omission). This was a substantial factor in the boy's death because he would have been immediately removed from his home had the worker informed police (actual cause). And it was foreseeable that the omission would result in continued abuse and possible death (proximate cause) (Choice C). But since murder requires malice aforethought, the worker's best defense is that he lacked that mental state.

(Choice B) Mistake or ignorance of the law is no defense to criminal liability (absent very narrow exceptions). Therefore, the worker could be convicted of murder even though he was unaware of the duty-to-report statute.

(Choice D) Under the doctrine of respondeat superior, an employer may be vicariously liable for a crime committed by its employee within the scope of employment and for the employer's benefit. Here, the supervisor recklessly advised the worker to keep quiet so that the day-care corporation could avoid a defamation suit. Therefore, the corporation may be vicariously liable for murder. But this is no defense to the worker's criminal liability.

Educational objective: A defendant is guilty of murder when his/her voluntary act or omission (1) actually and proximately caused another's death and (2) was committed with malice aforethought. An omission is the failure to perform a legal duty when the defendant could have reasonably done so.



选项正确率统计：A选项 59%（正确选项），B选项 3%，C选项 25%，D选项 11%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

谋杀罪（Murder）是指怀有预谋恶意（malice aforethought）（一种犯罪意图）而非法杀害他人（一种犯罪行为）。非法杀人可由自愿行为（例如，故意扣动枪的扳机）引起。但它也可能由不作为（omission）引起——即在被告有合理能力履行的情况下，未能履行法定的或其他法律义务。因果关系必须同时满足：
  • 事实上的因果关系（actual cause）——(1) 若无被告的行为，受害人当时不会死亡，或 (2) 当存在多个原因时，被告的行为是导致受害人死亡的实质性因素；并且
  • 法律上的因果关系（proximate cause）——死亡是被告行为的自然且可预见（ie, foreseeable）的后果。


在本案中，该工作人员未能履行其向警方报告男孩频繁出现瘀伤和伤痕的法定义务，尽管他有合理能力这样做（不作为）。这是导致男孩死亡的一个实质性因素，因为如果该工作人员通知了警方，男孩本会被立即从家中带离（事实上的因果关系）。并且，可以预见到该不作为将导致持续的虐待和可能的死亡（法律上的因果关系）（选项 C）。但是，由于谋杀罪需要有预谋恶意，该工作人员的最佳辩护理由是他缺乏这种犯罪意图。

（选项 B）对法律的错误理解或无知不能作为免除刑事责任的抗辩理由（极少数例外情况除外）。因此，即使该工作人员不知道有报告义务的法规，他仍可能被判谋杀罪。

（选项 D）根据“上级责任”（respondeat superior）原则，雇主可能因其雇员在雇佣范围内为雇主利益而实施的犯罪行为承担替代责任。在本案中，主管鲁莽地建议该工作人员保持沉默，以便日托公司可以避免诽谤诉讼。因此，该公司可能对谋杀罪承担替代责任。但这并不能成为该工作人员免除刑事责任的抗辩理由。

教学目标：当被告的自愿行为或不作为 (1) 在事实上和法律上造成他人死亡，并且 (2) 是在怀有预谋恶意的情况下实施的，则被告构成谋杀罪。不作为是指在被告有合理能力履行的情况下，未能履行一项法律义务。

MBE 刑法考点解析

不作为犯罪与谋杀意图
最佳论点：选项 A 他缺乏实施该罪行所必需的犯罪意图 (Mental State)。
核心考点：不作为谋杀 (Murder by Omission)

要判定某人因“不作为”构成谋杀罪，检方必须证明以下三个要素：

  • 法律义务 (Legal Duty)：被告有作为的法律义务（如本案中的法规）。
  • 因果关系 (Causation)：不作为导致了死亡。
  • 犯罪意图 (Mens Rea)：被告具有“预谋恶意” (Malice Aforethought)。
深度解析：为什么 A 是最佳辩护？
关键点 攻击“预谋恶意” (Malice)

谋杀罪是普通法中最严重的杀人罪，它要求被告具有特定的心理状态。在本案中，工作人员虽然没有报警，但他确实向主管报告了情况。

这一行为表明他并非对孩子的生命漠不关心。谋杀罪所需的恶意通常包括：
1. 杀人意图；
2. 造成严重身体伤害的意图；
3. 极度鲁莽/弃绝人性的冷漠 (Depraved Heart)。

工作人员听从主管建议虽然可能构成疏忽 (Negligence) 甚至鲁莽 (Recklessness)，但这更符合过失杀人 (Involuntary Manslaughter) 的标准，而不足以证明谋杀罪所需的“恶意”。因此，这是他最有力的辩护。

为什么其他选项不是最佳辩护？
选项 B 不知法 (Ignorance of Law)

Ignorantia juris non excusat（不知法不免责）。虽然他不知道有报告义务的法规，但这通常不能作为抗辩理由。只要法规存在，义务就存在。

选项 C 因果关系 (Causation)

题目中设定了一个非常具体的条件：法规规定“应立即将任何疑似受虐儿童从其家中带离”。

这意味着，如果他报了警，孩子就会被带走，也就不会死。这建立了直接的事实因果关系 (But-for Cause)。同时，不报告导致虐待升级致死也是可预见的，因此法律因果关系 (Proximate Cause) 也成立。攻击因果关系很难成功。

选项 D 替代责任 (Vicarious Liability)

虽然公司可能因主管的行为承担责任，但这并不免除直接行为人（工作人员）的个人刑事责任。刑事责任通常是个人的。

MBE 考试技巧

当题目问“最佳辩护 (Best Argument)”时，通常意味着被告可能在某些方面确实有过错，你需要找到检方证据链中最薄弱的一环。

在涉及严重犯罪（如谋杀）时，犯罪意图 (Mens Rea) 往往是区分重罪（Murder）和轻罪（Manslaughter）的关键。如果被告的行为显示出某种程度的关心（如报告给主管），通常很难证明其具有“弃绝人性的冷漠”。
